The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately shall bear, as part of the approval marking, a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.

The horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of: (a) direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12; (b) front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps; (c) reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.

Lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamp system shall bear the additional letter "Y" to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.

The single approval mark of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may be located anywhere on the lamps provided that it is visible after their installation.

The single approval mark of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may be located anywhere on the lamps provided that no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.

selected.text: Front/rear position lamps (A, R1, R2) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally (20°/80° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).

Front/rear end-outline marker lamps (AM, RM1, RM2) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).

Stop lamps (S1, S2) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard horizontally (20°/45° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).

Unless specified otherwise, the luminous intensity in the various directions of measurement shall be at least the minimum intensities shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (mathematically rounded down to three significant digits), H = 0°, V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis; however, for front and rear direction indicator lamps, front and rear position lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, parking lamps, stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS and side marker lamps intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

For reversing lamps, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions.

Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c, 12 shall meet, in the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities shown in Figure A3-I as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8.
Reversing lamps shall meet, in the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.

From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the differences of mass-produced lamps from the approved type shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

For conformity of production, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. on any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

translated.text: Each lamp forming part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear position lamp P-01, stop lamp P-02, reversing lamp P-03, and the integral rear retro-reflector P-05) shall satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of another UN Regulation. [UN R148 para. 3.2.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed in para. 3.2.2. Confirm whether evidence of separate approval (R148 for P-01/P-02/P-03, R150 for P-05) is acceptable.
Confirm the arrangement of the rear position lamp and stop lamp: grouped or reciprocally incorporated.
Confirm that the retro-reflector P-05 will be approved under UN R150 (Class IA or IB).

translated.text: Any lamp that does not satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of another UN Regulation shall not be part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp unit. [UN R148 para. 3.2.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed in para. 3.2.2.
Confirm that no other light-emitting or reflecting element (e.g. a logo or decorative lighting) is integrated in the unit without approval under a UN Regulation.

translated.text: Each light signalling function of the lamp shall be identified by the symbol specified in UN R148 para. 3.2.4, Table 1: rear position lamp R1 (steady) or R2 (variable); stop lamp S1 (steady) or S2 (variable); reversing lamp AR (the letters A and R may be mingled). [UN R148 para. 3.2.4, Table 1]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Select the rear position lamp class (R1 steady or R2 variable) and the stop lamp class (S1 steady or S2 variable).
Confirm whether the end-outline marker lamp symbol (RM1/RM2) is also to be claimed for the rear position lamp.

translated.text: Every device belonging to the approved lamp type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in UN R148 paras. 3.3.3.2 to 3.3.3.6. [UN R148 para. 3.3.1.1]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
'Sufficient size' is not quantified beyond the 'a' ≥ 5 mm rule of para. 3.3.1.2. Define the marking area and which part carries it (lens P-04 or housing P-08).

translated.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible. [UN R148 para. 3.3.1.1.1]
open_questions: No test method for legibility or indelibility is prescribed in the provided text.
Define the marking process (e.g. moulded-in or laser) and the acceptance criteria.

translated.text: The dimension 'a' of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm. [UN R148 para. 3.3.1.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The definition of dimension 'a' refers to the approval mark layout examples (annex), which are not provided.

translated.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, consisting of a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.1]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The approving Contracting Party and its distinguishing number have not yet been determined.

translated.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number prescribed in UN R148 para. 3.2.3.2. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The sequential number is assigned at approval and is not yet known.

translated.text: The four- to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
'Close to' is not quantified in the regulation.

translated.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying each light signalling lamp function prescribed in UN R148 para. 3.2.4 (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp). [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.3]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Depends on the final selection of R1/R2 and S1/S2 (see R148-base-0003).

translated.text: The approval marking shall include the number of the Regulation followed by the letter 'R' (i.e. '148R') and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time the approval is issued. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.4]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Confirm the series of amendments that will be in force at the time of approval.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately): The lamp shall bear, as part of the approval marking, a horizontal arrow showing the position in which the lamp is to be mounted. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.1]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: is the lamp side-specific (left/right handed) or mountable on either side?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp bears the horizontal mounting arrow per para. 3.3.2.5.1): For the rear position lamp function, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.1.1 (b); parent R148-base-0012]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Depends on the side-specific mounting decision.
Case (b) also covers rear end-outline marker lamps. Confirm whether the RM designation is claimed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the reversing lamp has reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps and the lamp bears the horizontal mounting arrow): For the reversing lamp function, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.1.1 (c); parent R148-base-0012]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: standard or reduced reversing lamp light distribution.
Case (a), direction indicators, is not relevant: the product has no direction indicator function.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps): The lamp shall bear the additional letter 'D' to the right of the function symbol specified in UN R148 para. 3.2.4. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: is any function intended for use as part of an assembly of two independent lamps? If so, which function(s)?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system): The lamp shall bear the additional letter 'Y' to the right of the function symbol specified in UN R148 para. 3.2.4. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: is any function part of an interdependent lamp system (e.g. a split lamp across the body and tailgate)?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp has reduced light distribution as defined in UN R148 Annex 3 para. 1.1): The lamp shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.3]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: reversing lamp with standard or reduced light distribution.
Annex 3 para. 1.1 is not provided.

translated.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.1]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.

translated.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Confirm the applicant's trade name or mark to be used.

translated.text: Because the lamp uses non-replaceable light sources, it shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or of the range of voltage. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.4]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The rated voltage or voltage range of the lamp has not been specified.
Confirm whether the lamp also includes electronic light source control gear, variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode. These also trigger this marking.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body): That control gear or variable luminous intensity control shall be marked with its identification number. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.6]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: is any control gear or variable intensity control located outside the lamp body?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body): That control gear or variable luminous intensity control shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.6]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Design decision pending: is any control gear or variable intensity control located outside the lamp body?

translated.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part of the lamp (outer lens P-04). [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.1]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Decide which part carries the marking (outer lens P-04 or housing P-08).
Confirm the lens-to-housing joint (with gasket P-09) is not designed to be separated.

translated.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle, or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened. Any prescribed LED substitute light source category shall be visible under the same conditions. [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.2]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The marking location relative to the vehicle body and tailgate/boot lid opening must be confirmed with the vehicle manufacturer.
The product uses non-replaceable LEDs. Confirm that no LED substitute light source category is prescribed, so that part does not apply.

translated.text: The approval marking and the markings of UN R148 paras. 3.3.3.2 (trade name or mark), 3.3.3.3, 3.3.3.4 (rated voltage), 3.3.3.5 (b) and 3.3.3.6 (where applicable) shall be affixed on the lamp. [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.5]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The contents of paras. 3.3.3.3 and 3.3.3.5 (b) are not in the provided obligations. Confirm their applicability to this lamp.

translated.text: The markings of UN R148 paras. 3.3.3.2 (trade name or mark), 3.3.3.3 (a), 3.3.3.4 (rated voltage), 3.3.3.5 and 3.3.3.6 shall not be required to fulfil the visibility-when-fitted requirement of para. 3.3.4.2. The approval marking remains subject to para. 3.3.4.2. [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.7; relaxation related to R148-base-0035]
open_questions: This is a permissive relaxation, not a test-based requirement; no verification method is prescribed.
The contents of paras. 3.3.3.3 (a) and 3.3.3.5 are not provided.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the single approval mark option is selected): Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations (e.g. R148 for the lamp functions and R150 for the retro-reflector), the lamp shall bear a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number. [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.1; permissive option]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Marking decision pending: single approval mark or separate approval marks.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if a single approval mark is used per para. 3.3.5.1): The single approval mark of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be located where it is visible after installation of the lamps. [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.1.1; parent R148-base-0041]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The installed visibility conditions depend on the vehicle integration.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if a single approval mark is used per para. 3.3.5.1): The single approval mark of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be located such that no light-transmitting part of the lamps can be removed without also removing the approval mark. [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.1.2; parent R148-base-0041]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
Confirm whether light-transmitting parts (outer lens P-04, retro-reflector P-05) are separable from the part carrying the mark.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if a single approval mark is used on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps): The size of each component of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval has been granted (e.g. R148 and R150). [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.2; parent R148-base-0041]
open_questions: Verification method is not prescribed.
The R150 minimum marking size requirements are not provided here and must be checked against R148 'a' ≥ 5 mm.

translated.text: Each lamp function submitted for approval under UN R148 (rear position lamp P-01, stop lamp P-02, reversing lamp P-03) shall conform to the requirements in paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.1]
open_questions: Para 4.1 does not prescribe a verification method; compliance is shown through the individual requirements of paras 4 and 5. Confirm the approval test plan.
Confirm class selection for each function: R1/R2, S1/S2, and AR standard or reduced distribution.

translated.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN R48 (and the Annexes referenced there), in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp. The requirements pertinent to each lamp function and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible. [UN R148 para 4.2]
open_questions: Which R48 series of amendments will be in force at the time of application?
Which R48 section 5/6 requirements are verifiable at lamp type approval for this lamp? Examples: apparent surface, geometric visibility, colour. The technical service must agree the list.
No verification method is prescribed in para 4.2.

translated.text: The lamp (including housing P-08, fasteners P-10, optical parts and LED PCB) shall be designed and constructed so that, in normal conditions of use and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.3]
open_questions: Para 4.3 prescribes no vibration test method, level or duration. What evidence will the technical service accept?
The drawing callout 'lamp stays aimed under vibration' is illustrative and not a regulatory criterion.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D'): the 'D' approval shall be used only for the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp functions (including rear end-outline marker lamp). It shall not be applied to the reversing lamp function, which is not among the functions listed. [UN R148 para 4.4.1]
open_questions: Will the 'D' option be chosen for the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp?
No verification method is prescribed; presumably checked by review of approval documentation and marking.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is approved as part of an interdependent lamp system marked 'Y'): the 'Y' approval shall be used only for the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp functions (including rear end-outline marker lamp). It shall not be applied to the reversing lamp function, which is not among the functions listed. [UN R148 para 4.4.2]
open_questions: Will the 'Y' option be chosen?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The rear position lamp function (P-01), when approved as a rear position lamp under UN R148, shall be regarded as also approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp. [UN R148 para 4.5.1]
open_questions: This is a deeming provision rather than a design obligation. Confirm whether any action is needed in the approval documentation.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The rear position lamp function (P-01), being grouped (or combined/reciprocally incorporated) with the stop lamp and reversing lamp, may also be used as a rear end-outline marker lamp. [UN R148 para 4.5.2]
open_questions: This is a permissive provision. Will the vehicle installation use P-01 as an end-outline marker lamp?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source and is designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted): this arrangement is permitted under UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.5.3]
open_questions: This is a permissive provision. Will a reciprocally incorporated rear position/stop lamp with a common LED light source and intensity regulation system be used?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp using a common light source): these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (e.g. a double filament light source), or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps. [UN R148 para 4.5.3.1]
open_questions: Which option, (a) or (b), will be chosen?
If (b), how will the vehicle tell-tale requirement be communicated? For example, through approval documentation.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (on request of the applicant, if a manufacturer logo is incorporated): the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of the lamp function may incorporate only one manufacturer logo, built by transparent or non-transparent components. This is permitted provided that all requirements of UN R148 for the specific function are fulfilled and the conditions of paragraph 4.5.5 (a) to (d) are met. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]
open_questions: The texts of conditions 4.5.5 (a) to (d) are not reproduced in the obligation set. Obtain and decompose them.
Will a logo be incorporated, and in which function? Note that obligation 0059 forbids logos in the stop and reversing lamps.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if a logo is incorporated): irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be incorporated in the apparent surface of the lamp. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]
open_questions: Which brand logo is intended?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if a logo is incorporated): the enclosed light emitting surface of the incorporated logo (including transparent and non-transparent components of the logo), in the direction of the reference axis, shall not exceed 100 cm2. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]
open_questions: No measurement method for the logo surface is prescribed in this obligation.
What logo dimensions are planned?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if a logo is incorporated): notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2 of UN R48, the logo light emitting surface (including transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) is not required to be symmetrical by itself. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]
open_questions: This is a permissive provision; there is no design obligation.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The stop lamp function (P-02) and the reversing lamp function (P-03) shall not incorporate a logo. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed; presumably checked by design review/inspection.
If the rear position lamp and stop lamp are reciprocally incorporated with a shared light-emitting surface, can a logo in the rear position lamp be allowed at all?

translated.text: In each single lamp function containing more than one LED light source, any group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source for the purposes of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.6.1.1]
open_questions: The LED circuit topology (series/parallel strings) for each function on P-07 must be defined to identify the 'light sources'.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp function containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3 of UN R148, and the maximum intensities are not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure is produced, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8, 6.7.8, 6.9.8, 6.10.8, 6.11.8, 6.12.8, 6.13.8 and 6.18.8 of UN R48, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure. [UN R148 para 4.6.1.2]
open_questions: Which option, (a) or (b), will be chosen for each function (rear position, stop, reversing)?
No single-failure test method is prescribed in this obligation. How will each light-source failure be simulated?
If (b), what is the failure signal interface to the vehicle?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if rear position lamp R2 and/or stop lamp S2 is chosen): in case of failure of the variable intensity control of an R2 (or RM2) or S2 lamp emitting more than the maximum value of category R1 (RM1) or S1 respectively, the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1 (RM1) or S1 respectively shall be fulfilled automatically. [UN R148 para 4.6.2]
open_questions: Will R2/S2 be chosen?
No test method for variable intensity control failure is prescribed in this obligation.

translated.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided no restriction on use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s). [UN R148 para 4.7.1]
open_questions: Will the LED modules on PCB be declared as non-replaceable light sources or as a light source module? The part mapping is unconfirmed.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The lamp, including the LED modules on PCB and driving circuitry (P-07), shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle. [UN R148 para 4.7.2.3]
open_questions: UN R148 prescribes no EMC test method or limits in this provision. Will compliance be demonstrated through UN R10 (ESA or vehicle level) evidence?
Is a separate R10 ESA approval for P-07 intended?

translated.text: Because the lamp is equipped with non-replaceable light sources (or light source modules), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp. [UN R148 para 4.8.1.2]
open_questions: This is a test-condition requirement. Confirm it is reflected in the test plan and lab instructions.

translated.text: If not otherwise specified, luminous intensities of each lamp function shall be measured with the light source continuously lit. [UN R148 para 4.8.1.7]
open_questions: This is a test-condition requirement. Are any other operating modes specified for any function?

translated.text: In case measurement results are challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation. [UN R148 para 4.8.1.8.3]
open_questions: This is a test-evaluation rule; there is no design obligation. Confirm the lab's application procedure.

translated.text: Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 6.75 V (6 Volt systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt systems) or 28 V (24 Volt systems). [UN R148 para 4.8.2]
open_questions: What is the vehicle system voltage? The product profile does not state 12 V or 24 V.
Is this provision overridden by 4.8.2.1/4.8.2.2 (operation as specified by the applicant) for this LED lamp?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control): the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant. [UN R148 para 4.8.2.1]
open_questions: Does the P-07 driving circuitry constitute electronic light source control gear?
What test operating conditions will the applicant specify?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and is equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s)): the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant. [UN R148 para 4.8.2.2]
open_questions: Which of 4.8.2.1 or 4.8.2.2 applies, given the P-07 driving circuitry?
What test operating conditions will the applicant specify?

translated.text: If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function (rear position, stop, reversing), the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity tests according to Annex 8 of UN R148 (per para 4.8.3.6), under the measurement conditions of para 4.8
open_questions: The minimum values are not reproduced in the obligation set. Obtain them from the para 5 tables for the selected classes (R1/R2, S1/S2, AR).
The drawing values (4 to 17 cd; 60 to 185 cd) are illustrative and must be checked against the para 5 tables.

translated.text: If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall not exceed, in any direction where the lamp is visible, the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity tests according to Annex 8 of UN R148 (per para 4.8.3.6), under the measurement conditions of para 4.8
open_questions: The maximum values are not reproduced in the obligation set. Obtain them from the para 5 tables for the selected classes.

translated.text: If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples outside the reference axis shall be not less than either: the minimum in the paragraph 5 table of the pertinent function multiplied by the percentage given for each direction in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3; or the intensity value given for each direction in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity tests according to Annex 8 of UN R148 (per para 4.8.3.6), under the measurement conditions of para 4.8
open_questions: The Annex 3 light distribution figures (standard or reduced for the AR function) must be identified for each function.

translated.text: If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2 of UN R148 shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity tests according to Annex 8 of UN R148 (per para 4.8.3.6), under the measurement conditions of para 4.8
open_questions: The Annex 2 geometric visibility angles and minimum values are not reproduced. Obtain them for each function. The drawing value '45° outboard' is illustrative.

translated.text: For each lamp function, the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 of UN R148 on local variations of luminous intensity shall be observed. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]
open_questions: The Annex 3 local variation provisions are not reproduced in the obligation set. Obtain and decompose them.
Does the Annex 8 test procedure (para 4.8.3.6) cover this, or is a separate method specified in Annex 3?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function is deemed to be a single lamp): the assembly shall comply with the maximum intensity requirements when all lamps together are lit. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.2]
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity tests according to Annex 8 of UN R148 (per para 4.8.3.6)
open_questions: Will the 'D' option be chosen, and for which function(s)?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function is deemed to be a single lamp): the assembly shall comply with the minimum intensity requirements when either lamp has failed. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.2]
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity tests according to Annex 8 of UN R148 (per para 4.8.3.6)
open_questions: Will the 'D' option be chosen, and for which function(s)?
How will lamp failure be simulated for the test?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system 'Y'): the interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements of UN R148 when all its interdependent lamps are operated together. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.3]
open_questions: Will the 'Y' option be chosen?
No verification method is prescribed beyond the general photometric/colorimetric tests.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if an interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a fixed component and partly on a movable component): the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s). The inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if these lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution at all fixed positions of the movable component(s). [UN R148 para 4.8.3.3]
open_questions: Is any part of the rear position lamp mounted on a movable component, such as a tailgate?
What fixed positions of the movable component apply?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if a variable intensity control is used, R2/S2): the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.4.1]
open_questions: Will R2/S2 be chosen?
No verification method is prescribed in this provision.
The para 5 ranges for R2/S2 are not reproduced in the obligation set.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (if a variable intensity control is used): the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 of UN R148 for the specific lamp. This applies under night-time conditions for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, and under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens) for other systems. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.4.2]
open_questions: Does the system depend only on day/night conditions, or on other conditions?
No verification method is prescribed in this provision.

translated.text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities of each lamp function shall be carried out according to Annex 8 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.6]
translated.verification_method: Annex 8 of UN R148
open_questions: The Annex 8 content is not reproduced in the obligation set. Obtain it for the test plan.

translated.text: The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function (red for rear position and stop lamps through outer lens P-04; white for reversing lamp through the clear window) shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3 of UN R148, applying the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. [UN R148 para 4.9]
translated.verification_method: Colour measurement inside the Annex 3 light distribution grid field for each function, applying the test procedure of UN R148 para 4.8
open_questions: The chromaticity limits for red and white are not stated in this obligation. Identify the applicable source, e.g. R148 para 5 or R48 para 2.30.
The drawing callout 'red, within the chromaticity limits' is illustrative.

translated.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3 of UN R148, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted by each lamp function shall be observed. [UN R148 para 4.9]
open_questions: No objective criterion for 'sharp variation of colour' or verification method is prescribed. How will the technical service assess it (e.g. visual observation)?

translated.text: The rear position lamp function (P-01), which is also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp, shall emit light such that each of the two samples submitted meets the requirements of UN R148 Table 4 (para 5.2.1).
open_questions: R148 para 5.2.1 does not set the photometric test method or conditions in this extract. Which Annex procedure (measuring distance, goniometer set-up, voltage/stabilisation conditions) applies?
Will the lamp be approved as R1 or R2? This decides which Table 4 row applies (see R148-base-0114 / R148-base-0115).

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp: the rear position lamp shall be permitted a luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane (UN R148 para 5.2.1 exception to Table 4).
open_questions: Will the rear position lamp and stop lamp be grouped (separate LEDs and lenses) or reciprocally incorporated (shared LEDs and light-emitting surface)? This exception applies only if they are reciprocally incorporated.
No verification method is prescribed for this exception in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady): the rear position lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Is the rear position lamp R1 (steady) or R2 (variable)?
No test method is prescribed in the extract. Where is the minimum measured (reference axis / Figure A3-I points)?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady) and used as a single lamp: the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Will the lamp be a single lamp or an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D"?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady) and the lamp is marked "D": the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.5 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Will the "D" (assembly of two independent lamps) option be used?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady): the rear position lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Figure A3-I (measuring points and percentage values) is not included in the extract and must be obtained.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady): the rear position lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 5·10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Table A2-1 angle values are not included in the extract.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity): the rear position lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Is the rear position lamp R2 (variable)? Which control / variable intensity conditions apply during measurement?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity) and used as a single lamp: the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 4.2·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Single lamp or "D" assembly?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity) and the lamp is marked "D": the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.1·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Will the "D" option be used?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity): the rear position lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Figure A3-I is not included in the extract.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity): the rear position lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 5·10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.2.1, Table 4).
open_questions: Table A2-1 angle values are not included in the extract.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The rear position lamp (also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp) shall comply with the failure provisions of UN R148 paragraph 4.6 (para 5.2.6).
open_questions: The content of R148 para 4.6 (failure provisions) is not included in the extract. What are the specific failure-mode requirements for non-replaceable LED sources?
Will failure detection be handled internally or rely on a vehicle tell-tale signal?
No verification method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp (also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp) shall be red (UN R148 para 5.2.7).
open_questions: The red chromaticity coordinate limits and the colour measurement method are not included in the extract. Which R148 / referenced provision defines them?

translated.text: The stop lamp function (P-02) shall emit light such that each of the two samples submitted meets the requirements of UN R148 Table 7 (para 5.5.1).
open_questions: Will the stop lamp be approved as S1 or S2 (see R148-base-0135 / R148-base-0136)?
No photometric test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady): the stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Is the stop lamp S1 (steady) or S2 (variable)?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady) and used as a single lamp: the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Single lamp or "D" assembly?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady) and the lamp is marked "D": the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.30·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Will the "D" option be used?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady): the stop lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Figure A3-I is not included in the extract.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady): the stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 3·10^-1 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Table A2-1 angle values are not included in the extract.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Is the stop lamp S2? Which day/night control conditions apply during measurement?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity) and used as a single lamp: the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 7.30·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Single lamp or "D" assembly?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity) and the lamp is marked "D": the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.65·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Will the "D" option be used?
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: Figure A3-I is not included in the extract.
No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 3·10^-1 cd (day) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: The definition of the day condition / control signal is not included in the extract.
Table A2-1 angle values are not included in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 7·10^-2 cd (night) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
open_questions: The definition of the night condition / control signal is not included in the extract.
Table A2-1 angle values are not included in the extract.

translated.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of UN R148 paragraph 4.6 (para 5.5.6).
open_questions: The content of R148 para 4.6 is not included in the extract.
Will failure detection be handled internally or rely on a vehicle tell-tale signal?
No verification method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red (UN R148 para 5.5.7).
open_questions: The red chromaticity limits and the colour measurement method are not included in the extract.

translated.text: The reversing lamp function (P-03, category AR) shall emit light such that each of the two samples submitted meets the requirements of UN R148 Table 10 (para 5.8.1).
open_questions: No photometric test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices: the reversing lamp shall satisfy a photometric value of at least 2.5·10^1 cd at an angle of 30° inwards, with the photometric intensity permitted to be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards (UN R148 para 5.8.1).
translated.verification_method: Photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards (UN R148 para 5.8.1); the full measurement method is not specified in the extract.
open_questions: Will the reversing lamp be intended exclusively for pair installation (reduced light distribution, arrow marking)?
Is the 2.5·10^1 cd value required only at the 30° inward limit or throughout the verified field? The extract is ambiguous on this.

translated.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
open_questions: No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.00·10^2 cd in or above the h-plane (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
open_questions: No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 6.00·10^2 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
open_questions: No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.00·10^3 cd below 5°D (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
open_questions: No test method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-V (para 5.8.1, Table 10). Table 10 sets no geometric visibility intensity requirement for AR (N.A.).
open_questions: Figure A3-V is not included in the extract.
The drawing callout 'visible to 45° outboard' is not a Table 10 requirement. Does it come from R48 installation needs?

translated.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of UN R148 paragraph 4.6 (para 5.8.6).
open_questions: The content of R148 para 4.6 is not included in the extract.
No verification method is prescribed in the extract.

translated.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white (UN R148 para 5.8.7).
open_questions: The white chromaticity limits and the colour measurement method are not included in the extract.

translated.text: Production rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved under UN R148 (para 6.1).
open_questions: The conformity of production procedures (sampling, test frequency, approval authority checks) are not detailed in the extract.

translated.text: For production lamps, no measured value of the rear position, stop or reversing lamp functions shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148 (para 6.1.3).
open_questions: The production sampling plan and measurement method are not specified in the extract.

translated.text:
For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in UN R148 Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall correspond to Table 12 (para 6.1.3), as follows (required minimum → 20 per cent equivalent / 30 per cent equivalent):
- 7·10^-1 cd → 5·10^-1 cd / 3·10^-1 cd
- 6·10^-1 cd → 4·10^-1 cd / 2·10^-1 cd
- 3·10^-1 cd → 2·10^-1 cd / 1·10^-1 cd
- 7·10^-2 cd → 5·10^-2 cd / 3·10^-2 cd
- 5·10^-2 cd → 3·10^-2 cd / 2·10^-2 cd
open_questions: The extract does not state when the 20 per cent versus the 30 per cent equivalent column applies (e.g. first versus second sampling stage).
The production sampling plan and measurement method are not specified in the extract.

translated.text: [Part 1 of 2, horizontal angles] The rear position lamp function (P-01, class R1 or R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. Where the lamp is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal angles below the H-plane shall be 20° inboard and 80° outboard. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0223)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method for geometric visibility. Confirm the method to be applied (e.g. per R148 main text or Annex 2).
What H-plane mounting height above ground will the lamp have on the target M1 vehicle (below 750 mm or not)? This determines which horizontal angle set applies below the H-plane.
Has the R1 (steady) or R2 (variable intensity) class been selected?

translated.text: [Part 2 of 2, vertical angles] The rear position lamp function (P-01, class R1 or R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. The following exceptions apply: 15° above and 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above and 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0223)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method for geometric visibility. Confirm the applicable method.
What is the intended H-plane mounting height on the vehicle (below 750 mm, between 750 mm and 2,100 mm, or above 2,100 mm)? Is the lamp an optional lamp?

translated.text: [Part 1 of 2, horizontal angles] Where the rear position lamp function (P-01) is deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1/RM2), it shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard and 80° outboard. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0225)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method for geometric visibility.
Confirm whether demonstrating the R1/R2 angles (45° inboard / 80° outboard) is accepted as covering the RM1/RM2 angles, as stated in the applicability decision.

translated.text: [Part 2 of 2, vertical angles] Where the rear position lamp function (P-01) is deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1/RM2), it shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. The following exceptions apply: 15° above and 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above and 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0225)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method for geometric visibility.
What is the intended H-plane mounting height on the vehicle?

translated.text: [Part 1 of 2, horizontal angles] The stop lamp function (P-02, class S1 or S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. Where the lamp is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal angles below the H-plane shall be 20° inboard and 45° outboard. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0226)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method for geometric visibility.
What is the intended H-plane mounting height on the vehicle (below 750 mm or not)?
Has the S1 (steady) or S2 (variable intensity) class been selected?

translated.text: [Part 2 of 2, vertical angles] The stop lamp function (P-02, class S1 or S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. The following exceptions apply: 15° above and 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above and 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0226)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method for geometric visibility.
What is the intended H-plane mounting height on the vehicle?

translated.text: Unless specified otherwise, each lamp function (rear position lamp P-01, stop lamp P-02, reversing lamp P-03) shall produce, in the various directions of measurement, a luminous intensity of at least the minimum intensities shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV. These minima are expressed as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with H = 0°, V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis. Exception: for the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp and the S1/S2 stop lamp intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H-plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 1.1)
translated.verification_method: Photometric measurement in the directions of measurement defined in Annex 3 (Figures A3-I to A3-XV)
open_questions: The minimum required intensity values (base values for the percentages) are not included in the extracted obligation. Obtain them from the R148 tables for R1/R2, S1/S2 and AR.
What H-plane height will the manufacturer specify (at or below 750 mm or above), which determines whether the 5° downward verification limit applies?
The drawing callouts (4 to 17 cd, 60 to 185 cd) are marked illustrative. Confirm them against the R148 requirements.

translated.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid (Annex 3), the luminous intensity of each lamp function in each direction within a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall be at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding that direction. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 1.2)
translated.verification_method: Photometric measurement within the Annex 3 grid field
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a measurement density between grid lines. Confirm the approach with the Technical Service.

translated.text: For the reversing lamp function (P-03), if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no luminous intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 1.2)
translated.verification_method: Visual examination for substantial local variations; where these are found, intensity measurement between the directions of measurement
open_questions: The extracted text does not define criteria for 'substantial local variations'.

translated.text: The rear position lamp function (P-01, R1/R2, including its use as a deemed rear end-outline marker lamp) and the stop lamp function (P-02, S1/S2) shall each meet, in the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities shown in Figure A3-I, expressed as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 2.1)
translated.verification_method: Photometric measurement in the directions of measurement of Figure A3-I
open_questions: The minimum intensity values of Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are not included in the extracted obligations. Confirm the applicable values for the selected classes (R1/R2, S1/S2).
Maximum intensity requirements are not part of this obligation. Confirm where they are captured.

translated.text: The reversing lamp function (P-03, class AR) shall meet, in the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 2.5)
translated.verification_method: Photometric measurement relative to the axis of reference in the directions of Figure A3-V
open_questions: Has standard or reduced light distribution been selected for the reversing lamp? Figure A3-V values for the selected option need to be confirmed.
The Figure A3-V values are not included in the extracted text.

translated.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced lamps shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 4, para. 1.1)
open_questions: The extracted text does not prescribe a verification method or a numeric tolerance for mechanical/geometric conformity of production. Define the CoP inspection approach with the Approval Authority.

translated.text: For conformity of production, when the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8 are tested on any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3 of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 5 para. 1.2 as cited)
translated.verification_method: Photometric testing per paragraph 4.8 on a lamp chosen at random from production

Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.

selected.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
All logos in lamps that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.

Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF; however, when a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated functions and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, shall be installed such that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro-reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing these projections, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces does not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included in the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, they shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system; however, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

The maximum height of a lamp above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of a lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle; no account shall be taken of interior lighting devices nor of reversing projections.

With the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

selected.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if any), the side-marker lamps (if any) and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously; this does not apply while front and rear position lamps (and side-marker lamps combined or reciprocally incorporated with them) are switched ON as parking lamps, while side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators, while daytime running lamps are switched ON, or while the front position lamp function is substituted under paragraph 5.12.1.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed by this Regulation it may be replaced by an "operating" tell-tale.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by each lamp shall be as listed in the table of paragraph 5.15.
Reversing lamp: colour of light emitted shall be white.
Stop lamp: colour of light emitted shall be red.
Rear position lamp: colour of light emitted shall be red.
Rear retro-reflector, non-triangular: colour shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Rear direction-indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, responding simultaneously to one or more of the conditions of paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., are allowed subject to conditions (a) and (b) of paragraph 5.26.

The luminous intensity of variable-intensity rear direction-indicator lamps (2b), rear position lamps (R2) and stop lamps (S2), when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

In the entire intensity range of variable-intensity lamps (2b, R2, S2), the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

Increase and decrease of luminous intensity of variable-intensity lamps, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds and contamination of the light-emitting surface.

Independent of environmental conditions, a decrease of the luminous intensity of variable-intensity lamps, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m; an intensity decrease already activated may remain active as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h.
Stop lamps of category S4 and rear fog lamps of category F2 may produce variable luminous intensity, based on the conditions of paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., independently from the other lamps.
No sharp variation of luminous intensity shall be observed during transition of variable-intensity lamps.
It may be possible for the driver to set variable-intensity lamp functions to static luminous intensities.

For vehicles of categories M and N, with the electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the vehicle category, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices of paragraphs 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. which were type approved with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as approved; this does not apply to devices including an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light sources approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

For vehicles of categories M and N, in all electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the devices or functions of paragraphs 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent, with the electrical system in a representative constant voltage operating condition; this does not apply to devices including an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light sources approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may be located within the body of the device.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
An LED module does not need to be replaceable if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

All lamps (devices) installed on a vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation.
Light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

A device type approved according to any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulations Nos. 148, 149 and/or 150 is deemed equivalent to one approved according to the latest series when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ, and may then be fitted on the vehicle without any update of the device type approval documents and device markings.
Reversing lamps shall be present (mandatory) on motor vehicles and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4.
On motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm, one reversing lamp is mandatory and a second is optional.
Reversing lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Reversing lamps shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground; for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.

Reversing lamps shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle; however, the two optional devices of paragraph 6.4.2.2., if installed, may be fitted on the side of the vehicle provided paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. are fulfilled.
For reversing lamps installed at the rear, geometric visibility shall be ensured in the vertical direction defined by angle α (paragraph 2.10.7.) = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.

For reversing lamps installed at the rear, geometric visibility shall be ensured in the horizontal direction defined by angle β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device, and 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two.
Reversing lamps shall be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that it can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position in which operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system start/stop device is not in a position allowing operation of the propulsion system.
A tell-tale for reversing lamps is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories are mandatory on all categories of vehicles.
The number of stop lamps shall be two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device on all categories of vehicles.
Stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of S1 or S2 category stop lamps which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of an S3 or S4 category stop lamp shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of S1 or S2 category stop lamps.
In length, S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be at the rear of the vehicle.

Geometric visibility of S1 or S2 category stop lamps, horizontal angle: 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle; however, for S1 and S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Geometric visibility of S1 or S2 category stop lamps, vertical angle: 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Stop lamps shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A tell-tale for stop lamps is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Rear position lamps of R, R1 or R2 categories are mandatory.

The number of rear position lamps shall be two, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; this condition does not apply to the optional rear position lamps.

Rear position lamps shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
In length, rear position lamps shall be at the rear of the vehicle.

Geometric visibility of rear position lamps, horizontal angle: 45° inwards and 80° outwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Geometric visibility of rear position lamps, vertical angle: 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Rear position lamps shall be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.; however, if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction indicator, the rear position lamp on the relevant side, or its reciprocally incorporated part, may be switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
