selected.text: A closed-circuit tell-tale for rear position lamps is mandatory; this requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The closed-circuit tell-tale for rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamps is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
In all cases, the distance between the rear fog lamp and each stop lamp shall be greater than 100 mm.
Non-triangular rear retro-reflectors are mandatory on motor vehicles; on trailers they are optional provided that they are grouped together with the other rear light-signalling devices.

The number of non-triangular rear retro-reflectors shall be two, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

The point on the illuminating surface of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

Non-triangular rear retro-reflectors shall be mounted not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm above the ground (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s); 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
In length, non-triangular rear retro-reflectors shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
Geometric visibility of non-triangular rear retro-reflectors, horizontal angle: 30° inwards and outwards.

Geometric visibility of non-triangular rear retro-reflectors, vertical angle: 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Non-triangular rear retro-reflectors shall be oriented rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.

When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON; however, the rear position lamps may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON and may remain OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to Annex 13).

translated.text: [R48 §5.1] The rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector functions) shall be so fitted to the M1 vehicle that, under normal conditions of use (R48 §§2.3.10, 2.3.10.1 and 2.3.10.2) and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of R48.
open_questions: R48 §5.1 prescribes no vibration test method, level or acceptance criterion; how is retention of characteristics under vibration to be demonstrated?

The drawing callout 'lamp stays aimed under vibration' is illustrative only and is not a regulatory acceptance criterion; confirm the intended design target for P-10 fasteners and P-08 mounting holes.

translated.text: [R48 §5.1] When the rear combination lamp is fitted to the vehicle, it shall not be possible for the lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
open_questions: R48 gives no criterion or test for 'inadvertently maladjusted'; how will this be verified for the P-10 fastener / P-08 mounting design?

translated.text: [R48 §5.3] For each light-signalling function of the rear combination lamp, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
open_questions: The reference axis of each function is set by the applicant in the R148/R150 device approval; confirm the reference axis definitions for P-01, P-02, P-03 and P-05.
No measurement procedure is prescribed in §5.3 itself; confirm whether verification follows the conditions of §5.4 (R48-base-0018).

translated.text: [R48 §5.3] For each light-signalling function of the rear combination lamp (none being a side retro-reflector or side-marker lamp), the reference axis when fitted shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
open_questions: No measurement procedure is prescribed in §5.3 itself; confirm the verification approach.
Confirm the reference axis definitions for P-01, P-02, P-03 and P-05 from the device approvals.

translated.text: [R48 §5.3] Any specific instructions laid down by the manufacturer for fitting the rear combination lamp (light-signalling device) shall be complied with when the lamp is installed on the vehicle.
open_questions: Do manufacturer-specific fitting instructions exist for this lamp? If so, which document contains them?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.4] In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the installed rear combination lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in R48 §§2.3.10, 2.3.10.1 and 2.3.10.2, and, where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.
translated.verification_method: Vehicle unladen, placed on a flat horizontal surface, in the condition defined in R48 §§2.3.10, 2.3.10.1 and 2.3.10.2 (AFS in neutral state where an AFS is installed), as prescribed by R48 §5.4.
open_questions: Confirm whether manufacturer-specific instructions exist; if they do, they override this default condition.

translated.text: [R48 §5.5.1] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane. This is to be estimated from the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not from the edge of its illuminating surface.
open_questions: The product profile does not explicitly confirm LH/RH lamp variants forming a pair; confirm the pair configuration.
No verification method or tolerance is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.5.2] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane. This requirement does not apply to the interior structure of the lamp.
open_questions: Confirm that LH/RH lamps are mirror variants.
No verification method or tolerance is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.5.3] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed in R48 §5.5.3; confirm whether R148/R150 colorimetric approval results for both LH and RH lamps are to be used.

translated.text: [R48 §5.5.4] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This does not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
open_questions: 'Substantially identical' is not quantified in R48; what acceptance criterion applies?
The drawing values (4 to 17 cd, 60 to 185 cd) are illustrative and are not taken as requirements here.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.5.5] CONDITIONAL – if a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear combination lamp: only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
open_questions: Open option: will a manufacturer logo be integrated in the lens or light-emitting surface?
This is a vehicle-level count; how many logo-bearing lamps exist on the vehicle rear?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.5.5] CONDITIONAL – if a logo is incorporated in the rear combination lamp: the logo shall be a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo; all other logos in lamps are prohibited.
open_questions: Open option: is a logo incorporated, and whose logo is it?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.7.1] Where the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another in the rear combination lamp, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and any other applicable requirements shall be fulfilled for each function.
open_questions: Open option: are the rear position and stop lamps grouped or reciprocally incorporated?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.7.1.1] The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF. Exception: where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions that can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of those other functions shall be fulfilled when those reciprocally incorporated functions and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
open_questions: Open option: grouped vs reciprocally incorporated rear position/stop lamp determines whether the exception applies.
No verification method is prescribed in R48 §5.7.1.1; confirm whether R148 photometric/colorimetric approval tests are relied upon.

translated.text: [R48 §5.7.2.2] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of a single lamp as defined in R48 §2.4.11.1(b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked 'D' or two independent retro-reflectors: it shall be installed such that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps/retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing these projections, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm.
open_questions: Open option: is the lamp part of a 'D'-marked assembly?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.7.2.3] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of a single lamp as defined in R48 §2.4.11.1(d) (interdependent lamp system marked 'Y'): it shall fulfil the requirements of R48 §5.7.2.1.
open_questions: Open option: is the lamp part of a 'Y' interdependent lamp system?
The content of R48 §5.7.2.1 is not provided in the obligation set.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.7.2.3] Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included in the common lamp body (P-08) and/or have the common outer lens (P-04) of the rear combination lamp, they shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system. However, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
open_questions: Is any function band- or strip-shaped and intended to form part of a 'Y' system (conditional R48-base-0034/0061/0144)?

translated.text: [R48 §5.8] The maximum height above the ground of each installed lamp function shall be measured from the highest point, and the minimum height from the lowest point, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis. Where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
translated.verification_method: Measurement from the highest point (maximum height) and lowest point (minimum height) of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, as prescribed by R48 §5.8.
open_questions: The applicable height limits for each function (R48 §§6.4, 6.7, 6.10, 6.14) are not included in this obligation set.

translated.text: [R48 §5.8.1] For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height above the ground of each lamp function shall be measured from the H plane.
translated.verification_method: Height measured from the H plane, as prescribed by R48 §5.8.1.
open_questions: Is a reduction of geometric visibility angles (for low mounting height) intended for any function?
The conditions allowing reduction are in §6.x and are not provided.

translated.text: [R48 §5.8.3] The width position of each lamp function shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis, that is furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps. Where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
translated.verification_method: Determination from the apparent surface edges in the direction of the reference axis, as prescribed by R48 §5.8.3.
open_questions: The applicable width/spacing limits (R48 §§6.4, 6.7, 6.10, 6.14) are not included in this obligation set.

translated.text: [R48 §5.9] In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
open_questions: How does this interact with the variable-intensity open option (R48 §5.26) and the permitted variations of §5.9.2?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.9.2] Any variation of the photometric characteristics of a lamp function of the rear combination lamp in relation to ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is used to provide another lighting function, shall comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
open_questions: Which variations are intended (e.g. rear position/stop reciprocal incorporation, ambient-dependent intensity)?
The technical provisions are in R148 and are not provided here.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.10.1] Red light emitted by the rear combination lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle. No account is taken of interior lighting devices or of reversing projections.
open_questions: R48 §5.10.1 prescribes no verification method itself; confirm whether §5.10.4.1/§5.10.4.3 (R48-base-0057/0059) are used for verification.

translated.text: [R48 §5.10.4.1] There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red lamp functions of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp) when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (R48 Annex 4).
translated.verification_method: Observation by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle per R48 Annex 4; in case of doubt, R48 §5.10.4.3 (R48-base-0059) applies.
open_questions: The definition of Zone 1 in R48 Annex 4 is not provided here.
Does the red retro-reflector (P-05) fall under 'red lamp' for this check?

translated.text: [R48 §5.10.4.3] In case of doubt, compliance with R48 §§5.10.4.1 and 5.10.4.2 shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front by each red lamp function of the rear combination lamp, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
translated.verification_method: Luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front, as verified during lamp type approval, not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking vehicle body influence into account where applicable (R48 §5.10.4.3).
open_questions: Is a forward-direction intensity measurement included in the R148 approval test report?
How will vehicle body influence be assessed?
§5.10.4.2 (white light to the rear) is not in this obligation set; confirm its applicability to the reversing lamp.

translated.text: [R48 §5.11.1] The electrical connections of the rear position lamp function shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if any), the side-marker lamps (if any) and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously. This does not apply: while front and rear position lamps (and side-marker lamps combined or reciprocally incorporated with them) are switched ON as parking lamps; while side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; while daytime running lamps are switched ON; or while the front position lamp function is substituted under R48 §5.12.1.
open_questions: This is a vehicle wiring/switching requirement; define the interface responsibility between the lamp and the vehicle harness/BCM.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.11.2] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system: all light sources of the system shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
open_questions: Open option: is the lamp part of a 'Y' interdependent lamp system?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.13] Where R48 prescribes a closed-circuit tell-tale for a function of the rear combination lamp, that tell-tale may be replaced by an 'operating' tell-tale (permissive provision; no additional lamp-level obligation).
open_questions: The tell-tale provisions for the rear position lamp (R48 §6.10) are not in this obligation set; confirm whether a closed-circuit tell-tale is actually prescribed.
This is a vehicle-level provision; confirm responsibility.

translated.text: [R48 §5.14.1] The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp shall not be concealed. Only main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps may be concealed when not in use.
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed; confirm that no vehicle feature (e.g. tailgate trim or movable panel) conceals the lamp.

translated.text: [R48 §5.15] The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall be as listed in the table of R48 §5.15.
open_questions: The chromaticity coordinate limits are defined elsewhere (R48 §2 / R148/R150) and are not provided here.
No verification method is prescribed in R48 §5.15; confirm reliance on device approval colorimetry.

translated.text: [R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be white.
open_questions: The white chromaticity limits are not provided in this obligation set.
No verification method is prescribed; confirm reliance on R148 colorimetric approval of the clear reversing window.

translated.text: [R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp function (P-02) shall be red.
open_questions: The red chromaticity limits are not provided in this obligation set.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp function (P-01) shall be red.
open_questions: The red chromaticity limits are not provided in this obligation set.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be red.
open_questions: The red colour limits for retro-reflectors are not provided here; R150 governs.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.16.1] The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and non-triangular rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of R48.
open_questions: The individual numbers in R48 §§6.4, 6.7, 6.10 and 6.14 are not included in this obligation set.
What other rear lamps on the vehicle contribute to these counts?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.22] Each lamp function of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing) shall be operable when installed. A lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse. This deeming rule does not apply to the retro-reflector.
open_questions: How does this deeming rule apply to non-replaceable LED modules (see R48-base-0145)?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26] CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is of category R2 and/or the stop lamp is of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control: the control shall respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions of R48 §§5.26.1 and 5.26.2 and shall comply with conditions (a) and (b) of R48 §5.26 (see R48-base-0131 and R48-base-0132).
open_questions: Open option: steady vs variable intensity; the R2/S2 categories are not confirmed.
Is the variable intensity control located in the lamp or in the vehicle?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26(a)] CONDITIONAL – if variable-intensity rear position lamps (R2) and stop lamps (S2) are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated in the rear combination lamp: their luminous intensity shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
open_questions: 'Similar proportion' is not quantified.
Open option: variable intensity.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26(b)] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity (R2/S2) is used: throughout the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.
open_questions: Which prescribed ratio applies (e.g. stop/rear position ratio in R148) is not provided here.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26.1] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity (R2/S2) is used: any increase or decrease of luminous intensity in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light-emitting surface shall remain within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.
open_questions: The pertinent limits (R148) are not provided here.
Which sensors or vehicle signals trigger the variation?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26.2] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity (R2/S2) is used: independent of environmental conditions, a decrease of luminous intensity within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations shall be activated only while the vehicle speed is ≤ 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is ≤ 20 m. A decrease already activated may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is ≤ 50 km/h.
open_questions: Is this vehicle-speed/following-distance function implemented in the vehicle or in the lamp?
The pertinent intensity limits are not provided here.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26.3] CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is of category S4: it may produce variable luminous intensity based on the conditions of R48 §§5.26.1 and 5.26.2, independently of the other lamps (permissive provision).
open_questions: Is the stop lamp of this rear combination lamp actually category S4? The earlier analysis indicates S1/S2.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26.4] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity is used: no sharp variation of luminous intensity shall be observed during transitions of the variable-intensity lamp functions.
open_questions: 'Sharp variation' is not quantified in R48.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.26.4] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity is used: the driver may be enabled to set the variable-intensity lamp functions to static luminous intensities (permissive provision).
open_questions: Is a driver setting to static intensity intended? This is a vehicle HMI decision.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.27.1] CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp (§2.5.4) and/or rear position lamp (§2.5.7) functions were type approved with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode, or at a voltage requested by the applicant: for the M1 vehicle, with the electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the vehicle category, the voltage supplied at the device terminals shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as approved. This does not apply to devices that include an electronic light source control gear, to devices with a variable intensity control as part of the device, or to devices with only light sources approved according to UN R128.
open_questions: Open option: is the electronic light source control gear integrated on the PCB (exemption applies) or external?
What voltage was specified in the R148 approval?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.27.2] CONDITIONAL – in all electric power supply conditions not covered by R48 §5.27.1, with the M1 vehicle electrical system in a representative constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the stop lamp (§2.5.4) and rear position lamp (§2.5.7) functions shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent. This does not apply to devices that include an electronic light source control gear, to devices with a variable intensity control as part of the device, or to devices with only light sources approved according to UN R128.
open_questions: Open option: integrated vs external electronic light source control gear determines whether the exemption applies.
What is the vehicle system voltage (6/12/24 V)?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.27.2] CONDITIONAL – if a means of controlling the maximum voltage at the device terminals is required: it may be located within the body of the rear combination lamp (permissive provision).
open_questions: Is voltage control needed (see R48-base-0139), and is it to be located on the P-07 PCB or in the vehicle?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.28.1] When installed, there shall be no obstacle inside the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp, observed from infinity. No account is taken of obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.
open_questions: The geometric visibility angles for each function (R48 §§6.4, 6.7, 6.10, 6.14) are not included in this obligation set.
The '45° outboard' drawing callout is illustrative only.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.28.5] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system: the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
open_questions: Open option: is the lamp part of a 'Y' interdependent lamp system?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [R48 §5.29] The LED modules (P-07) of the rear combination lamp may be non-replaceable only if this is stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval (R148).
open_questions: Confirm that the R148 communication sheet will state that the LED modules are non-replaceable.
No verification method is prescribed; a documentary check of the communication sheet is implied but not specified.

translated.text: [R48 §5.30] Each lamp function of the rear combination lamp installed on the vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulation specified in the relevant subparagraphs of R48 §6 (per product description: R148 for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps; R150 for the non-triangular rear retro-reflector).
translated.verification_method: Device type approval according to the corresponding device Regulations specified in R48 §6 (R148 / R150).
open_questions: The relevant R48 §6 subparagraphs are not included in this obligation set; confirm the device Regulation for each function.
Retro-reflector class IA vs IB is still open.

translated.text: [R48 §5.30.1] CONDITIONAL – if the rear combination lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo: the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN R148.
translated.verification_method: Type approval according to UN R148.
open_questions: Open option: will a manufacturer logo be incorporated?

translated.text: [R48 §5.33] If the rear combination lamp is type approved according to a preceding series of amendments to UN R148 and/or R150, it is deemed equivalent to a device approved to the latest series when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ. It may then be fitted on the vehicle without any update of the device type approval documents and device markings.
open_questions: Which series of amendments of R148/R150 will the approvals be granted under, and what are the change indexes per function?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.1] The M1 motor vehicle on which the rear combination lamp is installed shall be fitted with a reversing lamp (presence mandatory). The reversing lamp function (P-03) of the rear combination lamp is intended to provide this mandatory reversing lamp.
open_questions: R48 does not prescribe a verification method in para 6.4.1. Confirm whether vehicle-level installation inspection during R48 type approval is the intended evidence.
Confirm that the vehicle manufacturer relies on P-03 to meet the mandatory reversing lamp requirement and not on a separate reversing lamp.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.2.1] On the M1 vehicle, one reversing lamp shall be fitted (mandatory); a second reversing lamp is optional. The reversing lamp function (P-03) counts towards this number.
open_questions: Will the vehicle have one or two reversing lamps, i.e. P-03 on one side only or on both left and right lamps? This determines which horizontal visibility angles apply under para 6.4.5.1 (R48-base-0304).
No verification method is prescribed. Confirm the evidence expected, for example the vehicle installation drawing or R48 approval documentation.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.2.3] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
open_questions: The product description states device approval under R148. Confirm the R148 series of amendments to be used and that the reversing lamp function is included in the approval.
No verification method is prescribed by R48 here. Confirm that the R148 type-approval certificate and approval marking are the accepted evidence.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.4.2] The reversing lamp function (P-03), as installed on the M1 vehicle, shall be positioned not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground. (The increased maximum of 1,400 mm permitted for categories N2G, N3G, M2G and M3G (off-road) does not apply to M1.)
open_questions: The mounting height depends on the vehicle installation position, which is not defined in the product data. Obtain the vehicle mounting position or height of the reversing lamp apparent surface.
No verification method is prescribed in para 6.4.4.2. Confirm the measurement basis and the vehicle load condition per the general R48 provisions.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.4.3] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle. (The exception allowing side fitting applies only to the two optional devices of para 6.4.2.2, provided paras 6.4.5.2 and 6.4.6.2 are fulfilled; it does not apply to this rear-mounted lamp.)
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed. Confirm that vehicle installation inspection is the accepted evidence.
Confirm that no optional side-mounted reversing devices under para 6.4.2.2 are part of this product scope.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.5.1] For the reversing lamp function (P-03) installed at the rear, geometric visibility shall be ensured in the vertical direction defined by angle α (para 2.10.7) = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed in para 6.4.5.1. Confirm the method for assessing geometric visibility, for example CAD analysis of the apparent surface against vehicle body obstructions per the R48 definitions.
Vehicle installation geometry (body cut-outs, adjacent panels) is needed to confirm that no obstruction occurs within the angles.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.5.1] For the reversing lamp function (P-03) installed at the rear, geometric visibility shall be ensured in the horizontal direction defined by angle β = 45° to the right and to the left if there is only one reversing lamp device, and 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two reversing lamp devices.
open_questions: Is the vehicle fitted with one or two reversing lamps? If only one, 45° to both right and left is required. The drawing callout 'reversing lamp visible to 45° outboard' covers only the two-device outward case, and the inward angle (30° or 45°) must also be confirmed.
No verification method is prescribed. Confirm the method for assessing geometric visibility, for example CAD analysis with vehicle body geometry.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.6.1] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be oriented rearwards.
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed. Confirm how orientation is demonstrated, for example the lamp reference axis relative to the vehicle in the installation drawing.
The fasteners (P-10) are intended to maintain aim. R48 here states only the orientation and no retention test or criteria. Confirm whether any separate requirement applies.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.7.1] The electrical connections of the reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be such that it can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position in which operation of the propulsion system is possible.
open_questions: This is a vehicle-level wiring and control requirement. Confirm the split of responsibility between the lamp supplier and the vehicle manufacturer, including the lamp connector pin assignment for the reversing function.
No verification method is prescribed. Confirm the expected evidence, for example the vehicle wiring diagram or a functional check at vehicle level.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.7.1] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system start/stop device is not in a position allowing operation of the propulsion system.
open_questions: Confirm whether the PCB electronics (P-07) contain any logic, delay or latching that could keep the reversing LEDs ON after the supply or reverse signal is removed. This affects compliance at the lamp level.
No verification method is prescribed. Confirm the vehicle-level functional verification approach.

translated.text: [UN R48 para 6.4.8] A tell-tale for the reversing lamp function (P-03) is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure shall be provided if required by the component regulation (UN R148).
open_questions: Does UN R148, in the applicable series, require failure indication for this reversing lamp with non-replaceable LED light sources? If yes, the lamp must provide a failure-detection signal to the vehicle and the vehicle must provide the tell-tale.
No verification method is prescribed. Confirm the split of responsibility between the lamp supplier and the vehicle manufacturer.

translated.text: The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with stop lamp devices of category S1 or S2; the stop lamp function (P-02) of the rear combination lamp provides this mandatory S1 or S2 category device. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.1]
open_questions: Is the P-02 stop lamp category S1 (steady intensity) or S2 (variable intensity)? The product data does not state this.
No verification method is prescribed in para. 6.7.1. How will compliance be demonstrated at vehicle installation approval?

translated.text: The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with two stop lamp devices of category S1 or S2. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.2]
open_questions: Will a left-hand and a right-hand variant of the rear combination lamp provide the two S1/S2 devices, or will another device provide them?
No verification method is prescribed. It needs to be defined at vehicle level.

translated.text: The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with one stop lamp device of category S3 or S4. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.2]
open_questions: The S3/S4 device is not part of this product. Where is the vehicle-level owner of this requirement recorded?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The stop lamp device (P-02) shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.2]
translated.verification_method: Type-approval to UN R7 (02 series or later) or UN R148 (00 series or later), as stated in the obligation
open_questions: The product description indicates R148. Confirm the series of amendments and the approval marking for the stop lamp function.

translated.text: On the M1 vehicle, the point on the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02), in the direction of the reference axis, that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.1]
open_questions: Vehicle body width and lamp installation position are not provided.
No verification method is prescribed in this paragraph.

translated.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02) shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 2,100 mm only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and the optional lamps are not installed. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.2.1]
open_questions: The installed mounting height of the lamp on the target vehicle is not provided.
No verification or measurement method is prescribed in this obligation text.

translated.text: The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of the vehicle's S3 or S4 category stop lamp shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamps (P-02). [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.2.2]
open_questions: What is the upper edge height of the P-02 apparent surface, and what is the S3/S4 lamp position on the vehicle?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: In length, the S1 or S2 category stop lamps (P-02) shall be at the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.4]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: As installed, the S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02) shall provide horizontal geometric visibility of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle. For S1 and S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.5]
open_questions: Installed height is not known, so it is unclear whether the below-750 mm reduction applies.
No verification method is prescribed in this paragraph.

translated.text: As installed, the S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02) shall provide vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal. Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°. Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the upward angle may be reduced to 5°. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.5]
open_questions: Installed height is not known, so it is unclear whether either reduction applies.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The stop lamps (P-02) shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.6]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: All stop lamps, including P-02, shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.7.1]
open_questions: Which of UN R13 or R13-H applies to the target M1 vehicle, and which braking signal is used?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: Where the device that starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate, the stop lamps (P-02) are permitted not to function. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.7.2]
open_questions: This is a permissive provision. Will the vehicle design use it?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: A tell-tale for the stop lamps is optional. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.8]
open_questions: Is a stop lamp tell-tale fitted on the target vehicle?

translated.text: If the component regulation (UN R148) requires it for the stop lamp (P-02), the vehicle shall be fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.8]
open_questions: Does UN R148 require a failure tell-tale for the P-02 stop lamp with non-replaceable LED light sources? This needs to be determined from the R148 approval.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with rear position lamps of category R, R1 or R2; the rear position lamp function (P-01) provides this mandatory device. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.1]
open_questions: Is P-01 category R, R1 or R2? This is not stated in the product data.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The number of rear position lamps on the M1 vehicle shall be two. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.2]
open_questions: Will left-hand and right-hand variants of the lamp provide the two rear position lamps?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The rear position lamps (P-01) shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.2]
translated.verification_method: Type-approval to UN R7 (02 series or later) or UN R148 (00 series or later), as stated in the obligation
open_questions: Confirm the R148 series of amendments and approval marking for the rear position lamp function.

translated.text: The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp (P-01), in the direction of the reference axis, that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. This condition does not apply to optional rear position lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.4.1]
open_questions: Vehicle width and lamp installation position are not provided.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The rear position lamps (P-01) shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 2,100 mm only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and the optional lamps are not installed. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.4.2]
open_questions: The installed mounting height is not provided.
No verification or measurement method is prescribed in this obligation text.

translated.text: In length, the rear position lamps (P-01) shall be at the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.4.3]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: As installed, the rear position lamp (P-01) shall provide horizontal geometric visibility of 45° inwards and 80° outwards. Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.5.1]
open_questions: Installed height is not known, so it is unclear whether the reduction applies.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: As installed, the rear position lamp (P-01) shall provide vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal. Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°. Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the upward angle may be reduced to 5°. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.5.1]
open_questions: Installed height is not known, so it is unclear whether either reduction applies.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The rear position lamps (P-01) shall be oriented rearwards. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.6]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The electrical connections of the rear position lamps (P-01) shall be in accordance with para. 5.11 of UN R48. Exception: if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction indicator, the rear position lamp on the relevant side, or its reciprocally incorporated part, may be switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.7]
open_questions: The content of para. 5.11 is not included in the provided obligations. Its detailed requirements need to be extracted.
The product has no direction indicator, so the exception appears not to apply. Confirm this.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The vehicle shall be fitted with a closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps (P-01). This requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.8]

No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps (P-01) shall be combined with that of the front position lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.8]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed.

No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The distance between the vehicle's rear fog lamp and each stop lamp, including P-02, shall be greater than 100 mm in all cases. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.11.9]
open_questions: The rear fog lamp location on the target vehicle is not provided.

No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The M1 motor vehicle shall be fitted with non-triangular rear retro-reflectors; the integral retro-reflector (P-05) provides this mandatory device. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.1]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The number of non-triangular rear retro-reflectors on the M1 vehicle shall be two. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.2]
open_questions: Will left-hand and right-hand lamp variants provide the two retro-reflectors?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be type-approved according to the requirements for Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.2]

open_questions: Is the retro-reflector Class IA or Class IB? This depends on the watertightness of the lamp and is not settled.
Confirm the R150 series of amendments and approval marking.

translated.text: The point on the illuminating surface of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.4.1]
open_questions: The retro-reflector is a small insert, so its lateral position within the lamp and on the vehicle needs to be confirmed.
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: The non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be mounted not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), and 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.4.2]
open_questions: Does the integration of P-05 in the rear combination lamp qualify as 'grouped' with rear lamps for the 1,200 mm limit? Confirm this against the R48 definitions.
The installed height is not provided.

Where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.5]

translated.text: The non-triangular rear retro-reflectors (P-05) shall be oriented rearwards. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.6]

open_questions: This is a permissive provision. Does the P-05 illuminating surface share any area with the apparent surfaces of P-01, P-02 or P-03?
No verification method is prescribed.

translated.text: [UN R48 rev. 9.3.0, para. 6.19.7.5; parent obligation R48-base-0614] When the daytime running lamps of the M1 vehicle are switched ON, the vehicle electrical installation shall switch ON the rear position lamp function (P-01) of the rear combination lamp. Exception: the rear position lamps may be switched OFF while the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain OFF, as long as the ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux, measured according to UN R48 Annex 13.
open_questions: UN R48 does not prescribe a verification method for this switching requirement. Which method should be used (e.g. vehicle-level functional inspection at type approval)? Annex 13 is prescribed only for measuring the 7,000 lux ambient light condition.

This is a vehicle-level switching requirement implemented by the vehicle wiring/control (outside the lamp). Who is responsible for showing compliance: the vehicle manufacturer or the lamp supplier? What must the lamp provide to support it (e.g. connector pin-out for independent activation of P-01)?
Will the vehicle use the optional exception (rear position lamps OFF with DRLs ON above 7,000 lux)? If so, which ambient light sensor will be used, and how will compliance with Annex 13 be shown?

translated.text: [UN R48 rev. 9.3.0, para. 6.19.7.5; parent obligation R48-base-0615] When the daytime running lamps of the M1 vehicle are switched ON, any other lamp(s) mentioned in UN R48 paragraph 5.11 that are part of this rear combination lamp may also be switched ON. Where such lamps are switched ON with the daytime running lamps, they may be switched OFF while the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain OFF, as long as the ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux, measured according to UN R48 Annex 13.
open_questions: This obligation is permissive ('may'), not mandatory. Will the vehicle use this option for any lamp of the combination lamp? If not, no design action may be needed.

Which functions of this rear combination lamp are covered by paragraph 5.11? The decision notes rear position lamps; the 5.11 list is not given in the obligation text and needs to be confirmed against the regulation.
UN R48 does not prescribe a verification method for this switching provision. Annex 13 is prescribed only for measuring the 7,000 lux ambient light condition.
This is a vehicle-level switching provision implemented outside the lamp. Who is responsible for showing compliance: the vehicle manufacturer or the lamp supplier?

translated.text: Per UN R48 (version 9.3.0) para. 6.27.9.1, the stop lamp function (P-02) of the rear combination lamp shall not be used for the answer-back signal. Para. 6.27.9.1 also excludes front fog lamps and rear fog lamps; those functions are not part of this product and are not covered by this requirement.
open_questions: R48 does not prescribe a verification method for para. 6.27.9.1. How will compliance be shown: vehicle wiring/BCM review, functional check of the answer-back sequence, or a declaration in the vehicle installation approval documents?

Does the target M1 vehicle use an answer-back signal (para. 6.27.9) at all? If so, which lamps does it use? The vehicle manufacturer or integrator needs to confirm this, because activation is controlled at vehicle level, not by the lamp.

If the stop lamp and rear position lamp are reciprocally incorporated and share LEDs at different intensities, how will the vehicle control logic ensure that no answer-back activation drives the stop-lamp intensity level? The grouped vs reciprocally incorporated configuration is still open.

Does the lamp's electrical interface (connector pin assignment and any on-PCB control gear or variable intensity control) let the stop-lamp circuit be driven separately from the other functions, so that the vehicle can exclude it from answer-back activation?

translated.text: Each production M1 vehicle approved pursuant to UN R48 and fitted with the rear combination lamp shall be so manufactured as to conform to the approved vehicle type by meeting the requirements set out in UN R48 paragraphs 5 and 6. As identified in the applicability analysis, this covers the installed rear position lamp (para 6.10), stop lamp (para 6.7), reversing lamp (para 6.4), non-triangular rear retro-reflector (para 6.14) and the grouping or reciprocal incorporation of these functions (para 5.7). [Source: UN R48 rev. 9.3.0, para 8.1, p. 82; obligation R48-base-0865; applies to the vehicle installation, so it reaches the lamp only indirectly]
open_questions: Para 8.1 does not prescribe a verification method. Confirm whether the conformity-of-production checks in the subsequent paragraphs of R48 para 8 and Annex 9 apply. These include checks of position, geometric visibility, orientation and colour, and of luminous intensity. Confirm also how they are allocated between the vehicle manufacturer and the lamp supplier.

Define the contractual split of CoP responsibility. The vehicle manufacturer holds the R48 approval. The lamp supplier is responsible for keeping colour, apparent surface, photometric axis, orientation and fixation (P-04, P-06, P-10) consistent with the approved vehicle type.

The paragraph 5 and 6 requirements that apply depend on unresolved design options. These are: rear position lamp and stop lamp as grouped versus reciprocally incorporated lamps; retro-reflector Class IA versus IB; steady versus variable intensity for the stop and rear position lamps; a single lamp versus a 'D' or 'Y' marked assembly; and whether a manufacturer logo is present. Confirm each option before deriving detailed CoP checks.
Confirm the location of the electronic light source control gear (integrated on the PCB or external to the lamp). This determines which para 5 electrical-connection provisions are checked during CoP.

The illustrative drawing callouts are not regulation-derived values and should not be used as CoP acceptance criteria without confirmation against the source requirements. They are 4 to 17 cd for the rear position lamp, 60 to 185 cd for the stop lamp, and visibility to 45° outboard for the reversing lamp.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies only if the rear position lamp and stop lamp functions share or overlap apparent surfaces behind the outer lens, i.e. grouped/reciprocally incorporated configuration per Annex 3 Part 7): Where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and '7b' is the apparent surface according to UN R48 paragraph 2.10.2, function F1 shall not be transparent to function F2. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 3 Part 7; parent R48-base-0866]
open_questions: Is the rear position / stop lamp relationship grouped (separate apparent surfaces) or reciprocally incorporated (shared apparent surface)? This decides applicability.
Which lamp functions are F1 and F2 in this design (e.g. stop lamp vs rear position lamp, or reversing lamp vs red functions)?
No verification method is prescribed. How will non-transparency of F1 to F2 be demonstrated (e.g. drawing review of apparent surfaces, visual inspection)?

translated.text: For conformity of production, the position in width, height and length of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp as installed on the M1 vehicle (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.1; parent R48-base-0904]
translated.verification_method: Conformity of production check of lamp position in accordance with UN R48 paragraphs 2.10.2, 2.10.3, 2.10.4, 2.3.3 and 5.4 (Annex 9 para 1.1).
open_questions: Vehicle mounting position and target vehicle are not defined in the product profile. Lamp position compliance depends on vehicle integration data from the vehicle manufacturer.

translated.text: For conformity of production, the angles of geometric visibility of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp as installed (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled. Exception: the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in UN R48 paragraph 5.3 for the mounting of light-signalling devices. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.2.1; parent R48-base-0905]
translated.verification_method: Conformity of production check of angles of geometric visibility in accordance with UN R48 paragraph 2.10.7 (Annex 9 para 1.2.1).
open_questions: The drawing callout 'reversing lamp visible to 45° outboard' is labelled illustrative. Are the applicable geometric visibility angles for each function (paras 6.4, 6.7, 6.10, 6.14) confirmed against the installed vehicle geometry?

translated.text: For conformity of production, the visibility towards the front of red light emitted or reflected by the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, red outer lens and red retro-reflector) shall comply with UN R48 paragraph 5.10. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.2.2; parent R48-base-0906]
open_questions: Annex 9 para 1.2.2 does not prescribe a verification method beyond reference to paragraph 5.10. How will the CoP check of red light visibility towards the front be performed?

translated.text: For conformity of production, the visibility towards the rear of white light emitted by the rear combination lamp shall comply with UN R48 paragraph 5.10. The reversing lamp is exempt from this restriction only to the extent that paragraph 5.10 itself provides. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.2.2; parent R48-base-0906]
open_questions: Annex 9 para 1.2.2 does not prescribe a verification method beyond reference to paragraph 5.10. How will the CoP check of white light visibility towards the rear be performed?
The exact wording of the paragraph 5.10 exceptions for reversing lamps needs to be confirmed against the regulation text, since it is not reproduced in the obligation.

translated.text: For conformity of production, with every lamp supplied by the vehicle electrical system switched on, the LED-powered rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp, and any associated tell-tales, shall function in accordance with UN R48 paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.4; parent R48-base-0916]
open_questions: Annex 9 para 1.4 specifies the condition 'with every lamp supplied by the vehicle electrical system switched on' but no detailed test procedure. Which CoP functional check method will be used?
Does the stop / rear position lamp use steady or variable luminous intensity control? This affects the applicable individual specifications.
Is the electronic light source control gear integrated on the PCB or external to the lamp?
Tell-tales are vehicle-side items. How is responsibility for them allocated between lamp supplier and vehicle manufacturer?

translated.text: For conformity of production, the presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, category of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp (red rear position lamp, red stop lamp, white reversing lamp and red rear retro-reflector) shall be such that the requirements of UN R48 paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.6; parent R48-base-0918]
open_questions: Annex 9 para 1.6 does not prescribe a verification method. How will the CoP check of presence, number, colour, arrangement and category be performed (e.g. visual inspection against approval documentation)?
Is the retro-reflector Class IA or Class IB? This is not settled and affects the applicable category.
Which stop lamp category applies (S1/S2)? It is not stated in the product profile.
Is the lamp a single lamp, part of a 'D' marked assembly, or part of a 'Y' interdependent lamp system? This affects the number and arrangement assessment.

selected.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, differences of mass-produced retro-reflective devices from the approved type shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

When testing the photometric performance of any mass-produced retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
Mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates.

When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured for β1 = β2 = 0° and a mirror effect is produced when slightly turning the device, the reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0° the RI of the retro-reflective device exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.

For testing the retro-reflection, retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4, using the CIE angular system.

selected.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA and IIIB retro-reflectors, from an observation distance of 10 metres.

Moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and of advance warning triangles of Type 1 shall withstand the heat resistance test: 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat (and cold) resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.

Retro-reflective devices, whether part of a lamp or not, and sample units of retro-reflective marking, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the water penetration test: immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface, repeated after turning through 180° (illuminating surface at the bottom, rear face covered by about 20 mm of water), followed immediately by immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device has not passed the test.

If visual inspection after the water penetration test does not reveal water or in case of doubt, the RI of retro-reflectors shall be measured by the method of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after lightly shaking the device to remove excess water from the outside.

selected.text: For retro-reflective devices of Classes IB and IIIB, as an alternative and at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture test and the dust exposure test of Part 3 of Annex 6 shall be applied.

In the moisture test (Classes IB and IIIB), the sample device shall be subjected to a solid cone water spray completely covering the device, directed downward at 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of the rotating test platform, with a precipitation rate at the device of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min.
In the moisture test (Classes IB and IIIB), the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1 during the water spray.
In the moisture test (Classes IB and IIIB), all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.

In the moisture test, if the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate) and 55 min OFF.
The water spray of the moisture test (Classes IB and IIIB) shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray, the rotation and water spray shall be turned off and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed before evaluation.
Upon completion of the drain period of the moisture test, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the device, or be formable by tapping or tilting the device.

selected.text: In the dust exposure test (Classes IB and IIIB), the device shall be exposed in a test chamber of max. 2 m3 internal volume charged with 3 to 5 kg of test dust consisting of fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84.
In the dust exposure test (Classes IB and IIIB), all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.

In the dust exposure test, the mounted device shall be placed no closer than 150 mm from a chamber wall (devices longer than 600 mm horizontally centred), and the test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for a duration of 5 hours, the dust being allowed to settle between agitation periods.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

selected.text: Retro-reflective devices must be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflective device to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked (testing of resistance to corrosion per ISO 9227:2017), particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

For the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to a saline mist for 50 hours, comprising two exposure periods of 24 hours each separated by a 2-hour interval during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

For mirror-backed moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the accessible rear face shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush, a cotton cloth soaked in the n-heptane/toluol mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 applied to it for one minute, left to dry, brushed again with the same brush, and the RI then measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. after the whole mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
