open_questions: The criterion for 'if necessary' is not defined in the obligation text. Does the retro-reflector contain essential metal components that can corrode?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – if necessary: after the corrosion test, the rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]
translated.verification_method: Rear face abrasive-strength test per Part 5 of Annex 6.
open_questions: The criterion for 'if necessary' is not defined in the obligation text. Is the prism rear face mirror-backed (metallised) and accessible, or are the prisms non-metallised TIR?

translated.text: The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective devices in Part 3 of Annex 4. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]
translated.verification_method: Stability-in-time test per Part 3 of Annex 4.

translated.text: The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]
translated.verification_method: Resistance to weathering test per Part 6 of Annex 6.

translated.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflectors (P-05) in each group shall have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.2.1, p.12]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetric evaluation per paragraph 5.1.5 after the paragraph 5.1.3.1 test sequence.
open_questions: The make-up of the sample 'groups' is not defined in the obligations provided.

translated.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflectors (P-05) in each group shall have an RI that satisfies paragraph 5.1.4. This is verified only at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.2.2, p.12]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement per paragraph 5.1.4 at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° (or all Annex 4 Part 1 paras 1.1/1.2 positions if necessary) after the paragraph 5.1.3.1 tests.
open_questions: What decides 'if necessary' for measuring in all Annex 4 Part 1 positions?

translated.text: For photometric measurement of the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05), only the illuminating surface shall be considered. This surface is defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and lies within a circle of 200 mm diameter. The illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm². The surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not reach this area. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.3, p.12]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed. How will the manufacturer document the outermost parts of the optical system (e.g. drawing in the approval documentation)?
The size of the P-05 prism insert relative to the 100 cm² / 200 mm limits needs to be confirmed.

translated.text: The RI values of the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05), measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, shall be equal to or greater than the values in Table 3, expressed in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1, p.12]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, compared against Table 3.

translated.text: At an angle of divergence of 20', the red Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall have an RI of at least 3.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, at least 2.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and at least 1.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1 Table 3, p.12]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at divergence 20' and the stated illumination angles.
open_questions: The drawing callout 'reflectivity at 5° angle of incidence' does not match Table 3. Should it be revised?

translated.text: At an angle of divergence of 1°30', the red Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall have an RI of at least 5·10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, at least 2.8·10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and at least 2.5·10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1 Table 3, p.12]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 at divergence 1°30' and the stated illumination angles.

translated.text: Within the solid angle that has the centre of reference as its apex and is bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall have no RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1, p.12]
open_questions: The obligation does not prescribe how compliance across the solid angle is verified, e.g. measurement points or scan between the boundary lines. Which approach will be used?

translated.text: When the night-time colour of the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) is tested according to paragraph 4.2.1, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48. The regulation text permits red, amber or white; red applies to this product. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.5.2, p.13]
translated.verification_method: Night-time colour test per paragraph 4.2.1, comparing trichromatic coordinates with the UN R48 red limits.
open_questions: Is the red colour provided by the prism material or by the red outer lens (P-04) acting as a filter? This affects the test sample configuration.
The specific UN R48 red chromaticity limits need to be retrieved from R48.

translated.text: The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C), assessed by visual inspection for distortion. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Heat test per Part 1 of Annex 6, 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by visual inspection for distortion.
open_questions: Acceptance criteria for 'distortion' are not quantified in the obligation text.

translated.text: After the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetry by visual inspection, with trichromatic coordinates measured in case of doubt; photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

translated.text: The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the water test (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Water test of 10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position, with visual inspection.
open_questions: Acceptance criteria for the visual inspection (e.g. water ingress) are not stated in the obligation text.
Confirm that this Table 4 water test is the water penetration test of Part 2 of Annex 6 cited in paragraph 5.1.3.1.

translated.text: After the water test, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetry and photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° after the water test.
open_questions: The colorimetry method for this step (visual vs trichromatic) is not specified for this row in the obligation text.

translated.text: The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the motor fuels test of Part 1 of Annex 7 (5 min), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Motor fuels test per Part 1 of Annex 7, 5 min, with visual inspection.

translated.text: The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the oils test of Part 2 of Annex 7 (5 min), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Oils test per Part 2 of Annex 7, 5 min, with visual inspection.

translated.text: After the motor fuels and oils tests of Annex 7, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetry and photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° after the fuels and oils tests.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – where the corrosion test is necessary per paragraph 5.1.3.1: the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, 2-hour interval, 24 hours), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Corrosion test per Part 4 of Annex 6: 24 h, 2 h interval, 24 h, with visual inspection.
open_questions: Are essential metal components susceptible to corrosion present in the retro-reflector? This decides whether the test applies.
Acceptance criteria for the visual inspection are not stated in the obligation text.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – where the rear face test is necessary per paragraph 5.1.3.1: the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the rear face test (1 min), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Rear face test (Part 5 of Annex 6 per para. 5.1.3.1), 1 min, with visual inspection.
open_questions: Is the rear face of P-05 mirror-backed (metallised) and accessible? This decides whether the test applies.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – where the rear face test is performed: after the rear face test, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetry and photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° after the rear face test.

translated.text: The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be subjected to the stability-in-time test of Part 3 of Annex 4. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Stability-in-time test per Part 3 of Annex 4.

translated.text: After the stability-in-time test of Part 3 of Annex 4, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetry by visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates; photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

translated.text: The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Resistance to weathering test per Part 6 of Annex 6.

translated.text: After the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
translated.verification_method: Colorimetry by visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates; photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

translated.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced units of the rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB, red) shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R150. [UN R150 Annex 2 para. 1.1, p.25]
open_questions: Annex 2 para. 1.1 does not prescribe a verification method or inspection frequency for mechanical/geometric conformity. Which conformity-of-production checks (dimensions, sampling plan) will be agreed with the Type Approval Authority?
Annex 2 does not define a numeric tolerance for 'inevitable manufacturing deviations'. Which dimensional tolerances from the approval drawings will serve as the reference?

translated.text: When the photometric performance of any randomly chosen mass-produced rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB) is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in UN R150. [UN R150 Annex 2 para. 1.2, p.25]
translated.verification_method: Photometric testing of randomly chosen mass-produced retro-reflective devices, with measured values compared against the R150 minimum values with a maximum unfavourable deviation of 20 per cent (Annex 2 para. 1.2).
open_questions: The applicable minimum CIL/RI values for red Class IA/IB are not included in this obligation set. Which R150 table and paragraph apply?
Annex 2 para. 1.2 does not specify sampling frequency or sample size. What will the conformity-of-production sampling plan be?

translated.text: Mass-produced units of the red rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed in UN R150. [UN R150 Annex 2 para. 1.3, p.25]
open_questions: Annex 2 para. 1.3 does not prescribe a verification method. Which colorimetric test procedure and sampling plan will be used for conformity of production?
The red chromaticity coordinates are not included in this obligation set. Which R150 paragraph defines them?
Is the red colour produced by the optical unit itself or by the red outer lens (P-04) acting as a filter? This determines which parts are included in the colour check (open option).

translated.text: When the RI of the rear retro-reflector (P-05) is measured for β1 = β2 = 0°, and a mirror effect is produced when the device is turned slightly, the reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°. [UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.1, p.28]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement according to UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.1. Where a mirror effect occurs at β1 = β2 = 0°, the reading is taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
open_questions: This is a test-procedure obligation. Will it be met by the technical service's test report, or does the manufacturer's in-house/CoP photometric procedure also need to follow it?

translated.text: If, for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0°, the RI of the rear retro-reflector (P-05) exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°. [UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.4, p.28]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement according to UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.4.
open_questions: The 'specified value' of RI for red Class IA/IB at β1 = β2 = 0° is not included in this obligation set. Which R150 table applies?

translated.text: For testing retro-reflection, the rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4, using the CIE angular system. [UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 3.3, p.30]
translated.verification_method: Retro-reflection measurement under CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) according to UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1, using the CIE angular system.
open_questions: Will in-house conformity-of-production photometric equipment also be required to use CIE Standard Illuminant A and the CIE angular system?

translated.text: The shape of the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB) shall not be easily confused, from an observation distance of 10 metres, with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA and IIIB retro-reflectors. [UN R150 Annex 5 para. 1.1, p.33]
translated.verification_method: Visual observation of the illuminating surface shape from an observation distance of 10 metres (Annex 5 para. 1.1).
open_questions: R150 does not define an objective criterion for 'not easily confused'. Who makes this judgement (the technical service), and is the current rectangular shape accepted?
Does the red outer lens (P-04) styling around the retro-reflector change the perceived shape of the illuminating surface?

translated.text: The moulded plastics reflector of the rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB, PMMA) shall withstand the heat resistance test: 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1, p.42]
translated.verification_method: Heat resistance test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1: 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then 1 hour cooling at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
open_questions: Will the test be run on the retro-reflector alone or on the retro-reflector integrated in the lamp (including P-04 outer lens if it acts as a filter)?

translated.text: After the heat resistance test of UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the rear retro-reflector (P-05), and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1 para. 3, p.42; acceptance criterion for R150-base-0210]
translated.verification_method: Visual inspection for cracking or appreciable distortion after the Annex 6 Part 1 heat resistance test (Annex 6 Part 1 para. 3).
open_questions: R150 gives no quantitative limit for 'appreciable distortion'. What acceptance basis will the technical service use?
The paragraph refers to the 'heat (and cold)' resistance test. Is a cold test also applicable to Class IA/IB, or only the 65 °C heat test of para. 1?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies when the water penetration test route is used, i.e. the watertight / Class IA option): The rear retro-reflector (P-05), whether part of a lamp or not, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the water penetration test. The test is: immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface; then repetition after turning the device through 180° (illuminating surface at the bottom, rear face covered by about 20 mm of water); then immediate immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.1, p.42]
translated.verification_method: Water penetration test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.1: 10 min immersion at 50 °C ± 5 °C with highest point of illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface; repeat after turning through 180° with rear face under about 20 mm of water; then immediate immersion under the same conditions at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
open_questions: Will the lamp housing containing the retro-reflector be declared watertight (Class IA) or not watertight (Class IB)? This decides whether this test or the Class IB moisture/dust alternative applies.
For a retro-reflector integrated in the combined lamp, what are the 'removable parts' to be stripped before the test?
The seal (P-09) callout 'no water ingress after the spray test' is not the R150 water penetration test. Is a separate R150 immersion test planned?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies when the water penetration test route of Annex 6 Part 2 is used, i.e. the watertight / Class IA option): After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the rear retro-reflector (P-05). If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device has not passed the test. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.2, p.42; acceptance criterion for R150-base-0213]
translated.verification_method: Visual inspection of the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit for water after the Annex 6 Part 2 water penetration test (Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.2).
open_questions: Is the class (IA watertight vs IB not watertight) confirmed? This determines whether this criterion applies.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies when the water penetration test route of Annex 6 Part 2 is used, i.e. the watertight / Class IA option): If visual inspection after the water penetration test does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the RI of the rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be measured by the method of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 of UN R150, after the device has been lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.3.1, p.42]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement by the method of UN R150 paragraph 5.1.3.2.2, after lightly shaking the device to remove external excess water (Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.3.1).
open_questions: The content of R150 para. 5.1.3.2.2 and the pass/fail criterion for the post-test RI measurement are not included in this obligation set. Which RI limit applies?
Is the class (IA watertight vs IB not watertight) confirmed? This determines whether this re-measurement applies.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies only if the P-05 retro-reflector is approved as Class IB, i.e. combined with a non-watertight lamp, and the manufacturer requests the alternative): the P-05 retro-reflective device shall be subjected to the moisture test and the dust exposure test of R150 Annex 6 Part 3, as an alternative to the water penetration test. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 1; parent R150-base-0222]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test and dust exposure test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3
open_questions: Is the lamp housing containing the retro-reflector watertight (Class IA) or not watertight (Class IB)? The P-09 seal design determines this.
If Class IB, will the manufacturer request the moisture/dust alternative instead of the standard water penetration test?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the moisture test, the sample device shall be subjected to a solid cone water spray that completely covers the device. The spray shall be directed downward at 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of the rotating test platform. The precipitation rate at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.1.3; parent R150-base-0223]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the moisture test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1 during the water spray. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.2; parent R150-base-0224]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the moisture test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open. Drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.1; parent R150-base-0225]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.
Does the lamp housing (P-08) have drain holes, vents or drain wicks? None are identified in the product profile.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected, and the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions): during the moisture test, the rear position lamp (P-01), stop lamp (P-02) and reversing lamp (P-03) functions shall be operated at design voltage. The operating cycle shall be 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate) and 55 min OFF. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.3; parent R150-base-0226]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.
Is the retro-reflector formally 'reciprocally incorporated' or 'grouped' with the lamp functions under the definitions?
What is the design voltage of the LED module/PCB (P-07)? It is not stated in the product profile.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): the water spray of the moisture test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min). [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.4; parent R150-base-0227]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): after the water spray, the rotation and water spray shall be turned off. The device shall then be allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed before evaluation. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.5; parent R150-base-0228]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): on completion of the moisture test drain period, no standing pool of water shall have formed in the interior of the device. No such pool shall be formable by tapping or tilting the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.6; parent R150-base-0229]
translated.verification_method: Moisture test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2, with inspection after the 1 h drain period including tapping/tilting
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): after the moisture test, the exterior of the device shall be dried with a dry cotton cloth. The RI of the device shall then be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 of R150. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.6; parent R150-base-0230]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement per UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 after the moisture test
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.
This excerpt gives no RI acceptance limit after the moisture test. Which limit applies (e.g. the Class IA/IB CIL values or a permitted reduction)?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the dust exposure test, the device shall be exposed in a test chamber of max. 2 m3 internal volume. The chamber shall be charged with 3 to 5 kg of test dust consisting of fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.2; parent R150-base-0231]
translated.verification_method: Dust exposure test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open. Drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.5; parent R150-base-0232]
translated.verification_method: Dust exposure test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.
Does the lamp have drain holes, vents or drain wicks?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the dust exposure test, the mounted device shall be placed no closer than 150 mm to a chamber wall; devices longer than 600 mm shall be horizontally centred. The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible for 2 to 15 s at 15 min intervals, over a total duration of 5 hours, and shall be allowed to settle between agitation periods. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.6; parent R150-base-0233]
translated.verification_method: Dust exposure test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.
Is the lamp longer than 600 mm (centring condition)? The lamp length is not stated.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): on completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth. The RI shall then be measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of R150. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.7; parent R150-base-0234]
translated.verification_method: RI measurement per UN R150 para 5.1.3.2.2 after the dust exposure test
open_questions: Applicability depends on the Class IA/IB decision and on selection of the moisture/dust alternative.
This excerpt gives no RI acceptance limit after the dust test. Which limit applies?

translated.text: The P-05 retro-reflective device shall be designed to retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 1; parent R150-base-0235]
translated.verification_method: Corrosion resistance test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 4 (ISO 9227:2017), as stated in the same paragraph
open_questions: Apart from the Annex 6 Part 4 corrosion test, is any other evidence expected to show retention of photometric/colorimetric characteristics under humidity?
Does the red outer lens (P-04) act as the filter of the retro-reflector, so that its colour retention is also covered?

translated.text: The resistance of the front surface of the P-05 retro-reflective device to tarnishing shall be checked by corrosion resistance testing per ISO 9227:2017. This check is required particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 1; parent R150-base-0236]
translated.verification_method: Corrosion resistance test per ISO 9227:2017 as referenced in UN R150 Annex 6 Part 4
open_questions: Does the retro-reflector contain essential metal components (e.g. metallised mirror backing)? Is the aluminium-metallised P-06 reflector considered part of the retro-reflective device?

translated.text: The resistance to deterioration of the protection of the rear face of the P-05 retro-reflective device shall be checked by corrosion resistance testing per ISO 9227:2017. This check is required particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 1; parent R150-base-0236]
translated.verification_method: Corrosion resistance test per ISO 9227:2017 as referenced in UN R150 Annex 6 Part 4
open_questions: Does the retro-reflector rear face have a protection (e.g. mirror backing/coating)? This is an open design option: mirror-backed vs TIR prisms.

translated.text: For the corrosion test, the complete rear combination lamp (since P-05 is combined with lamps) shall be stripped of all removable parts. It shall then be subjected to a saline mist for 50 hours: two exposure periods of 24 hours each, separated by a 2-hour interval during which the sample is allowed to dry. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 2; parent R150-base-0237]
translated.verification_method: Corrosion test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 4
open_questions: Which parts of the lamp count as 'removable parts' to be stripped (e.g. fasteners P-10)?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if the retro-reflective device has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion): the saline mist for the corrosion test shall be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 3; parent R150-base-0238]
translated.verification_method: Corrosion test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 4
open_questions: Are essential metal components susceptible to corrosion present in the retro-reflector (open design option)?
If no such components are present, which saline mist specification applies?

translated.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall show no signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 4.1; parent R150-base-0239]
translated.verification_method: Inspection immediately after the corrosion test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 4
open_questions: The regulation does not quantify 'excessive corrosion'. What is the assessment criterion, or is it left to Technical Service judgement?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL (applies if P-05 is a mirror-backed moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB with an accessible rear face): the accessible rear face shall be treated in this sequence: (1) brushed with a hard nylon brush; (2) a cotton cloth soaked in the n-heptane/toluol mixture defined in Annex 7 Part 1 applied to it for one minute; (3) left to dry; (4) brushed again with the same brush. The whole mirror-backed rear face shall then be covered with Indian ink, and the RI measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 5 para 3; parent R150-base-0241]
translated.verification_method: Rear face resistance test per UN R150 Annex 6 Part 5, with RI measurement per para 5.1.3.2.2
open_questions: Is the P-05 prism insert mirror-backed (metallised), and is its rear face accessible (open design option)?
This excerpt gives no RI acceptance limit after the rear face test. Which limit applies?

translated.text: The outer surface of the P-05 retro-reflective device, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol. After about five minutes the surface shall show no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are not objected to. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 7 Part 1 para 1.1; parent R150-base-0247]
translated.verification_method: Resistance to fuels test per UN R150 Annex 7 Part 1
open_questions: Is the 'outer surface' of the retro-reflective device the red PMMA outer lens (P-04) covering the prism insert, or the P-05 insert itself?

translated.text: Since P-05 is a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB, its outer surface, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes. The RI shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of R150. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 7 Part 2 para 1.1; parent R150-base-0251]
translated.verification_method: Resistance to lubricating oils test per UN R150 Annex 7 Part 2, with RI measurement per para 5.1.3.2.2
open_questions: This excerpt gives no RI acceptance limit after the lubricating oil test. Which limit applies?
Is the outer surface the P-04 outer lens or the P-05 insert?

translated.text: In the R150 approval mark of the P-05 retro-reflective device, the approval number shall be placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E"; it may be in any position in relation to that circle. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 10; parent R150-base-0284]
open_questions: The verification method is not prescribed in the regulation. Is inspection of the approval mark artwork/sample acceptable?
Will the R150 mark be grouped with the R148 lamp marks on the outer lens or housing?

translated.text: In the R150 approval mark of the P-05 retro-reflective device, the digits constituting the approval number shall face the same way as the letter "E". [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 10; parent R150-base-0285]
open_questions: The verification method is not prescribed in the regulation. Is inspection of the approval mark acceptable?

translated.text: In the R150 approval mark of the P-05 retro-reflective device, the group of symbols indicating the class (IA or IB) shall be diametrically opposite the approval number. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 10; parent R150-base-0286]
open_questions: The verification method is not prescribed in the regulation. Is inspection of the approval mark acceptable?
Is the class symbol IA or IB? This depends on the watertightness decision.

The ESA sample(s) submitted for approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the type designation.

Where an ESA is (part of) a light source, it shall either hold an approval according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128, or be demonstrated by a Technical Service test report to be not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128; otherwise approval according to Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.

For vehicle approval by testing of individual ESAs, all relevant electrical/electronic systems or ESAs (paragraph 3.1.3.) shall be approved in accordance with this Regulation and installed in accordance with any conditions attached to their approval.

selected.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation; no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle.
Approval markings on ESAs need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation (configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA representative of its type on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 1.
The positive transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall not exceed +75 V (vehicles with 12 V systems) or +150 V (vehicles with 24 V systems).
The negative transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall not exceed -100 V (vehicles with 12 V systems) or -450 V (vehicles with 24 V systems).

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9, with the test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band given in Table 2a and the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band given in Table 2b.

ESA radiated immunity test level in over 90 per cent of the frequency band shall be, depending on the Annex 9 method used: stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).

ESA radiated immunity minimum test level over the whole frequency band shall be, depending on the Annex 9 method used: stripline 50 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).
During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the ESA's "immunity related functions".

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The ESA starting profile test shall be evaluated according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for ESA immunity test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor (starting profile not applicable otherwise), the ESA shall withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems), 10 pulses, achieving functional status B for ESAs related to immunity related functions which shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESAs related to immunity related functions, and D for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses, achieving FPSC III whether or not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses, achieving FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses, achieving FPSC II for ESAs related to immunity related functions and FPSC III for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.

selected.text: During the ESA immunity test, the ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA absorber chamber immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-2 using the substitution method to establish the test field conditions, with vertical polarization.

The vehicle limits in paras 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.3.2.1, 6.3.2.2, 7.2.2.1 and 7.2.2.2 cited in the same paragraph apply to vehicles, not to this ESA.]
open_questions: The obligation requires measured disturbance levels but does not itself prescribe the measurement method, sample size or frequency for CoP. Which method applies (e.g., the ESA test annexes referenced by paras 6.5/6.6), and what sampling will be used?

Will the LED drive be passive or active (switching/PWM/microcontroller)? With a passive drive, the para 6.10 exceptions may relieve narrowband/broadband emission testing, which affects how this CoP requirement is applied.
Is para 7.10.2.1 applicable? Per the earlier analysis it is expected not to be, since there is no REESS charging mode.

translated.text: For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp ESA taken from the series, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user, when in the state defined in UN R10 Annex 6, paragraph 4, and subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in UN R10 paragraph 6.8.2.1 and, if applicable, 7.18.2.1 for ESAs. This applies in particular to the immunity related functions: stop lamp (P-02) and rear position lamp (P-01). [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.2, p.26; obligation R10-base-0193]
open_questions: The obligation references the vehicle state of Annex 6 para 4 while being applied to an ESA. Which ESA test state and test method (e.g., the ESA immunity annex referenced by para 6.8) will be used for CoP?

What observable degradation criteria will be applied for the stop lamp and rear position lamp functions at bench level (e.g., unintended on/off, flicker, intensity change)? These are not defined in this obligation.
Is the reversing lamp function (P-03), which is not in the immunity-related function list, to be monitored during CoP immunity testing?
CoP sampling plan and frequency are not prescribed in this obligation.
Is para 7.18.2.1 applicable? Per the earlier analysis it is expected not to be, since there is no REESS charging mode.

translated.text: For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp approved as a component or STU and taken from the series, the lamp shall show no degradation of performance of 'immunity related functions' (stop lamp P-02 and rear position lamp P-01) up to the conducted disturbance levels given in UN R10 paragraph 6.9.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.3, p.26; obligation R10-base-0194]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed in this obligation. Is the conducted transient immunity test per the annex referenced by para 6.9.1 (Annex 10) to be used for CoP, and with which sampling plan?
Will the supply voltage be 12 V or 24 V? The applicable conducted disturbance levels in para 6.9.1 depend on the supply voltage.
Which acceptance criteria define 'no degradation of performance' for the stop and rear position lamp functions?
Is para 7.19.1 applicable? Per the earlier analysis it is expected not to be, since there is no REESS charging mode.

translated.text: For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp approved as a component or STU and taken from the series, the conducted transient emission of the lamp shall not exceed the levels given in UN R10 paragraph 6.7.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.3, p.26; obligation R10-base-0195]
open_questions: No verification method is prescribed in this obligation. Is the conducted transient emission test per the annex referenced by para 6.7.1 (Annex 10) to be used for CoP, and with which sampling plan?
Will the supply voltage be 12 V or 24 V? This determines the applicable emission levels in para 6.7.1.
Does a passive LED drive design invoke any para 6.10 exception affecting this test?
Is para 7.17.1 applicable? Per the earlier analysis it is expected not to be, since there is no REESS charging mode.

translated.text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry, P-07), shall not exceed a broadband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 30 MHz to 75 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.5.2.1, Appendix 6; parent obligation R10-base-0206]
open_questions: The obligation text does not specify the test method, antenna distance or detector type. Confirm the ESA broadband measurement method referenced from para 6.5 (applicable annex) before defining verification.

Confirm whether the para 6.10 exceptions (e.g. ESA without active switching) could deem the lamp compliant with the broadband limits. This depends on the open LED drive topology (passive/linear vs switch-mode/PWM/microcontroller).

translated.text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry, P-07), shall not exceed a broadband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 75 MHz to 400 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.5.2.1, Appendix 6; parent obligation R10-base-0206]
open_questions: The obligation text does not specify the test method, antenna distance or detector type. Confirm the ESA broadband measurement method referenced from para 6.5 (applicable annex).
Confirm whether the para 6.10 exceptions apply to the broadband limits for the chosen LED drive topology.

translated.text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry, P-07), shall not exceed a broadband radiated electromagnetic interference level of 63 dBµV/m (120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 400 MHz to 1,000 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.5.2.1, Appendix 6; parent obligation R10-base-0207]
open_questions: The obligation text does not specify the test method, antenna distance or detector type. Confirm the ESA broadband measurement method referenced from para 6.5 (applicable annex).
Confirm whether the para 6.10 exceptions apply to the broadband limits for the chosen LED drive topology.

translated.text: Where the LED drive electronics of the rear combination lamp (P-07) are not deemed to comply under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10 (e.g. an active electronic driver with an oscillator, switch-mode/PWM or microcontroller), the lamp as an ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 30 MHz to 75 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.6.2.1, Appendix 7; parent obligation R10-base-0208]
open_questions: The LED drive topology (passive/linear vs active switching/microcontroller) is an open design option, and it determines whether this limit applies or the para 6.10 exception is used.
The obligation text does not specify the test method, antenna distance or detector type. Confirm the ESA narrowband measurement method referenced from para 6.6 (applicable annex).
Clarify whether the 'square component' on the PCB is an oscillator, microcontroller or driver IC.

translated.text: Where the LED drive electronics of the rear combination lamp (P-07) are not deemed to comply under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10, the lamp as an ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 75 MHz to 400 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.6.2.1, Appendix 7; parent obligation R10-base-0208]
open_questions: The LED drive topology is an open design option, and it determines whether this limit applies or the para 6.10 exception is used.
The obligation text does not specify the test method, antenna distance or detector type. Confirm the ESA narrowband measurement method referenced from para 6.6 (applicable annex).

translated.text: Where the LED drive electronics of the rear combination lamp (P-07) are not deemed to comply under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10, the lamp as an ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated electromagnetic interference level of 53 dBµV/m (120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 400 MHz to 1,000 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.6.2.1, Appendix 7; parent obligation R10-base-0209]
open_questions: The LED drive topology is an open design option, and it determines whether this limit applies or the para 6.10 exception is used.
The obligation text does not specify the test method, antenna distance or detector type. Confirm the ESA narrowband measurement method referenced from para 6.6 (applicable annex).

translated.text: When installed on the M1 vehicle and subjected to the UN R10 vehicle immunity test in 50 km/h mode with dipped beams ON (manual mode), the rear lamp's rear light (rear position lamp function, P-01) shall not go OFF. Going OFF constitutes failure of the immunity test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, Annex 6 para 2.1.1.1, Table '50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions', p.72; obligation R10-base-0244]
translated.verification_method: Vehicle immunity test per UN R10 Annex 6, 50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions (para 2.1.1.1), with dipped beams ON (manual mode); failure criterion: lighting goes OFF (front light and rear light).
open_questions: This is a vehicle-level test criterion (Annex 6). The earlier analysis states that vehicle-level sections concern the vehicle manufacturer. Confirm whether the lamp supplier must demonstrate this, e.g. by supporting the vehicle test or by an ESA-level equivalent, or whether it is a flow-down requirement only.

The obligation covers both front light and rear light. The front light (dipped beams) is outside this product's scope and is assigned to the vehicle manufacturer or front lamp supplier. Confirm this allocation.
Confirm which of the product's functions count as 'rear light' for this criterion. The rear position lamp is assumed. The reversing lamp and stop lamp are not assumed to be ON in this mode.
Field strength, frequency range and other test parameters are not stated in this obligation. They must be taken from the rest of Annex 6 and not assumed here.

source.paragraph: Annex 6 2.1.1.1. Table 50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions

translated.text: When installed on the M1 vehicle and subjected to the UN R10 vehicle immunity test in 50 km/h mode with the brake pedal not depressed, the rear lamp's stop lamp function (P-02) shall not activate unexpectedly. Unexpected activation of the stop lights constitutes failure of the immunity test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, Annex 6 para 2.1.1.1, Table '50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions', p.72; obligation R10-base-0257]
translated.verification_method: Vehicle immunity test per UN R10 Annex 6, 50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions (para 2.1.1.1), brake pedal not depressed; failure criterion: unexpected activation of the brake or unexpected activation of the stop lights.
open_questions: The obligation also covers unexpected activation of the brake. That is a vehicle braking-system matter outside this lamp's scope. Confirm it is allocated to the vehicle manufacturer.
This is a vehicle-level test criterion (Annex 6). Confirm the supplier's verification responsibility, e.g. support of the vehicle test or an ESA-level equivalent.
Confirm whether the stop lamp control is discrete wired or via a data bus (open option in the earlier analysis). This affects which ESA the vehicle test exercises.
Test parameters such as field strength and frequency range are not stated in this obligation. They must be taken from the rest of Annex 6.

source.paragraph: Annex 6 2.1.1.1. Table 50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions

translated.text: When installed on the M1 vehicle and subjected to the UN R10 vehicle immunity test in brake mode, the rear lamp's stop lamp function (P-02) shall not be inactivated at any time during the mode. Brake mode means: the vehicle is in a state allowing the braking system to operate normally, the parking brake is released, vehicle speed is 0 km/h, and the brake pedal is depressed to activate the brake function and stop lights without any dynamic cycle. Inactivation of the stop lights during the mode constitutes failure of the immunity test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, Annex 6 para 2.1.1.1, Table 'Brake mode vehicle test conditions', p.72; obligation R10-base-0259]
translated.verification_method: Vehicle immunity test per UN R10 Annex 6, brake mode vehicle test conditions (para 2.1.1.1); failure criterion: stop lights inactivated during the mode, or brake warning light ON with loss of brake function.
open_questions: The obligation also includes the failure criterion 'brake warning light ON with loss of brake function'. That concerns the vehicle braking system and telltale, not this lamp. Confirm it is allocated to the vehicle manufacturer.
This is a vehicle-level test criterion (Annex 6). Confirm the supplier's verification responsibility, e.g. support of the vehicle test or an ESA-level equivalent.
Test parameters such as field strength and frequency range are not stated in this obligation. They must be taken from the rest of Annex 6.

source.paragraph: Annex 6 2.1.1.1. Table Brake mode vehicle test conditions

translated.text: The broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA (P-07 LED modules on PCB with drive circuitry and wiring/connector) shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in UN R10 Annex 7. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 1.2; parent R10-base-0292]
translated.verification_method: Test: broadband emission measurement per CISPR 25 as specified in UN R10 Annex 7
open_questions: Which CISPR 25 edition is referenced by UN R10 v7.2.0, and which test house or Technical Service will perform the test?

translated.text: During the UN R10 Annex 7 broadband emission test, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 2.1; parent R10-base-0293]
translated.verification_method: Test: operating condition of the ESA during the Annex 7 broadband emission test
open_questions: The regulation does not define 'normal operation mode' or 'maximum load' for this lamp. Which combination of rear position, stop and reversing functions should be energised simultaneously, and at what supply voltage? This needs to be agreed with the Technical Service.

translated.text: Because the rear lamp ESA is not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', its broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0298]
translated.verification_method: Test: ALSE method per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 (UN R10 Annex 7 para 3.1)

translated.text: The rear lamp ESA shall comply with the ESA broadband emission limits of UN R10 para 6.5 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS). [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 4.1; parent R10-base-0301]
translated.verification_method: Test: broadband emission measurement per UN R10 Annex 7, compared against para 6.5 limits
open_questions: The numeric broadband limit values of para 6.5 are not in the supplied obligation set and must be taken from the regulation text.

translated.text: The ESA broadband emission limits of UN R10 para 6.5 shall be treated as quasi-peak detector limits. Measurements of the rear lamp ESA may use quasi-peak or peak detectors; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 4.2; parent R10-base-0302]
translated.verification_method: Test: broadband emission measurement with a quasi-peak detector, or a peak detector with the 20 dB CISPR 12 correction (UN R10 Annex 7 para 4.2)
open_questions: Which detector type will the test laboratory use? Confirm how the 20 dB correction is applied as defined in CISPR 12.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required for the rear lamp ESA, i.e. the selected LED drive electronics are not deemed compliant under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10 (open option: passive vs active driver). Where it applies, the narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in UN R10 Annex 8. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 1.2; parent R10-base-0303]
translated.verification_method: Test: narrowband emission measurement per CISPR 25 as specified in UN R10 Annex 8
open_questions: Which LED drive concept is selected: passive drive, or active switch-mode/PWM/microcontroller driver?
The decision cites an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz as the trigger. Confirm the exact para 6.10 exception criteria against the regulation text.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the UN R10 Annex 8 narrowband emission test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 2; parent R10-base-0304]
translated.verification_method: Test: operating condition of the ESA during the Annex 8 narrowband emission test
open_questions: Is the active driver option selected?
How are 'normal operation mode' and 'maximum load' defined for this lamp, i.e. which functions are energised? This needs agreement with the Technical Service.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the narrowband emission test of the rear lamp ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0305]
translated.verification_method: Test: ALSE method per CISPR 25 para 6.4 (UN R10 Annex 8 para 3.1)
open_questions: Is the active driver option selected?

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the rear lamp ESA shall comply with the ESA narrowband emission limits of UN R10 para 6.6 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 4.1; parent R10-base-0306]
translated.verification_method: Test: narrowband emission measurement per UN R10 Annex 8, compared against para 6.6 limits
open_questions: Is the active driver option selected?
The numeric narrowband limit values of para 6.6 are not in the supplied obligation set and must be taken from the regulation text.

translated.text: CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the narrowband emission measurements of the rear lamp ESA shall be performed with an average detector. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 4.2; parent R10-base-0307]
translated.verification_method: Test: narrowband emission measurement with an average detector (UN R10 Annex 8 para 4.2)
open_questions: Is the active driver option selected?

translated.text: The rear lamp ESA, which is not in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', shall demonstrate compliance with the ESA immunity requirements using any combination of the following methods, at the manufacturer's discretion: absorber chamber (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline (ISO 11452-5) and reverberation chamber (ISO 11452-11). The chosen combination shall cover the full frequency range specified in UN R10 Annex 9 para 3.1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 1.2.1; parent R10-base-0308]
translated.verification_method: Test: ESA immunity testing per UN R10 Annex 9 using the selected ISO 11452 method(s), with a frequency coverage check
open_questions: Which combination of immunity test methods will be selected, and how is the frequency range split between them?

The immunity levels and functional performance criteria of UN R10 para 6.8 for the immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) are not in the supplied obligation set and must be taken from the regulation text.

translated.text: The immunity test conditions for the rear lamp ESA, including frequency range and general test conditions, shall be according to ISO 11452-1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 2.1; parent R10-base-0310]
translated.verification_method: Test: ESA immunity test conditions per ISO 11452-1 (UN R10 Annex 9 para 2.1)
open_questions: Which ISO 11452-1 edition is referenced by UN R10 v7.2.0?

translated.text: During the immunity test, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 2.2; parent R10-base-0311]
translated.verification_method: Test: operating condition of the ESA during UN R10 Annex 9 immunity testing
open_questions: The regulation does not specify how to stimulate the lamp. Should the stop lamp and rear position lamp (immunity-related functions) and the reversing lamp be energised simultaneously or separately, and how will function be monitored? This needs agreement with the Technical Service.

translated.text: Immunity measurements of the rear lamp ESA shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time chosen according to ISO 11452-1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0317]
translated.verification_method: Test: ESA immunity measurement over 20 to 6,000 MHz per UN R10 Annex 9 para 3.1 and ISO 11452-1

translated.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal modulation for the rear lamp ESA shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0318]
translated.verification_method: Test: ESA immunity test signal modulation per UN R10 Annex 9 para 3.1
open_questions: Will any deviating modulation be agreed with the Technical Service?

translated.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal modulation for the rear lamp ESA shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0319]
translated.verification_method: Test: ESA immunity test signal modulation per UN R10 Annex 9 para 3.1
open_questions: Will any deviating modulation be agreed with the Technical Service?

translated.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal modulation for the rear lamp ESA shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0320]
translated.verification_method: Test: ESA immunity test signal modulation per UN R10 Annex 9 para 3.1
open_questions: Will any deviating modulation be agreed with the Technical Service?
The 380–400 MHz band overlaps the 20–400 MHz AM range of R10-base-0318. How is the overlap to be handled? Clarify against the regulation text or with the Technical Service.

translated.text: Where the absorber chamber method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-2, using the substitution method to establish the test field conditions and with vertical polarization. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.1.2; parent R10-base-0321]
translated.verification_method: Test: absorber chamber immunity test per ISO 11452-2, substitution method, vertical polarization
open_questions: Will the absorber chamber method be part of the selected combination of immunity methods?

translated.text: Where the TEM cell method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell, depending on the ESA to be tested. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.2.2; parent R10-base-0324]
translated.verification_method: Test: TEM cell immunity test per ISO 11452-3
open_questions: Will the TEM cell method be used?
Should field coupling be maximised to the ESA or to the wiring harness for this lamp?

translated.text: Where the bench bulk current injection method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, using either the substitution method with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA or the closed loop method with the injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.3.2; parent R10-base-0325]
translated.verification_method: Test: bulk current injection immunity test per ISO 11452-4 (substitution at 150 mm or closed loop at 900 mm)
open_questions: Will the BCI method be used, and with the substitution or the closed loop method?

translated.text: As an alternative to the bench BCI test, the rear lamp ESA may be tested for bulk current injection immunity while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4. In that case the substitution method shall be used with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.3.2; parent R10-base-0326]
translated.verification_method: Test: in-vehicle bulk current injection immunity test per ISO 11451-4, substitution method, probe at 150 mm
open_questions: Will the in-vehicle BCI alternative be used, and is a representative M1 vehicle available to the component manufacturer?

translated.text: Where the stripline method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.4.2; parent R10-base-0328]
translated.verification_method: Test: stripline immunity test per ISO 11452-5
open_questions: Will the stripline method be used?

translated.text: Where the reverberation chamber method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11, using a test setup with ground plane unless otherwise specified. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.5.2; parent R10-base-0329]
translated.verification_method: Test: reverberation chamber immunity test per ISO 11452-11 with ground plane setup
open_questions: Will the reverberation chamber method be used?

translated.text: (Part 1 of 2: immunity) The rear lamp ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, as tested according to UN R10 Annex 10. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 1; parent R10-base-0330]
translated.verification_method: Test: conducted transient immunity per UN R10 Annex 10
open_questions: The immunity performance criteria and test levels (UN R10 para 6.9 and the ISO 7637-2 / ISO 16750-2 severity levels) are not in the supplied obligation set and must be taken from the regulation text.

translated.text: (Part 2 of 2: emission) Conducted transients from the rear lamp ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited, as tested according to UN R10 Annex 10. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 1; parent R10-base-0330]
translated.verification_method: Test: conducted transient emission per UN R10 Annex 10
open_questions: The applicable conducted transient emission limits are not in the supplied obligation set and must be taken from the regulation text.

translated.text: Test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0331]
translated.verification_method: Test: ISO 7637-2 test pulse 1 (UN R10 Annex 10 para 2)
open_questions: Is the supply voltage 12 V or 24 V?
Which lamp connections (e.g. separate stop, position and reversing feed inputs, or a bus interface) count as 'operationally connected to supply lines'?
The test levels and required functional status are not in the supplied obligation set.

translated.text: Test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0332]
translated.verification_method: Test: ISO 7637-2 test pulse 2a (UN R10 Annex 10 para 2)
open_questions: Is the supply voltage 12 V or 24 V?
Which lamp connections count as 'operationally connected to supply lines'?
The test levels and required functional status are not in the supplied obligation set.

translated.text: Test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0333]
translated.verification_method: Test: ISO 7637-2 test pulse 2b (UN R10 Annex 10 para 2)
open_questions: Is the supply voltage 12 V or 24 V?
Which lamp connections count as 'operationally connected to supply lines'?
The test levels and required functional status are not in the supplied obligation set.

translated.text: Test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0334]
translated.verification_method: Test: ISO 7637-2 test pulse 3a (UN R10 Annex 10 para 2)
open_questions: Is the supply voltage 12 V or 24 V?
Which lamp connections count as 'operationally connected to supply lines'?
The test levels and required functional status are not in the supplied obligation set.

translated.text: Test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0335]
translated.verification_method: Test: ISO 7637-2 test pulse 3b (UN R10 Annex 10 para 2)
open_questions: Is the supply voltage 12 V or 24 V?
Which lamp connections count as 'operationally connected to supply lines'?
The test levels and required functional status are not in the supplied obligation set.

translated.text: The starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. Exception: ESAs reserved exclusively for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor are not subject to the starting profile. The rear lamp is intended for M1 vehicles generally and is not so reserved. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0336]
translated.verification_method: Test: ISO 16750-2 starting profile (UN R10 Annex 10 para 2)
open_questions: Confirm that the lamp is not reserved exclusively for electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor.

selected.text: The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; this does not apply to parts protruding less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; the hardness shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle, and where a Shore A measurement is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.1. to 5.5. shall apply in addition to the particular specifications of paragraph 6., except where these particular specifications expressly provide otherwise.
